description: Repo-realignment program WS1 CHECKPOINT 1 — the centralization the user has repeatedly asked for, begun. tools/registry.py: the ONE unifying reader for name/descriptor/quantity vocabulary, resolve(term) -> {term, kind, key, registry_key, via, disagreement}. Built as a FACADE that DELEGATES to the three existing resolvers (tools/names.py, tools/descriptor_registry.py, tools/quantity_registry.py) BY IDENTITY — no vocabulary data moved, no existing file touched, zero blast radius. This is the load-bearing 'one reader' step; the eventual WS1 end-state flips the delegation (data moves into references/registry/ *.yaml and the old resolvers become thin shims over this reader) in later, higher-blast-radius checkpoints. references/registry/README.md (Status: PROPOSED) documents the target partitioned package (names/descriptors/entities/glossary/aliases/deprecated_terms/vocabulary) and the evidence-based fold-in order (frozen/dead registries first, then live-by-reference). Built via an agonist(producer)/antagonist(critic) subagent pair (CLAUDE.md section 10). The antagonist confirmed the core SOUND — reuse-by-identity verified by `is` (not just asserted), CWD-independence, no short-circuit (all three resolvers queried every call so disagreement is a real query), 23 tests pass — and found defects, ALL reconciled: (HIGH) 'Influence' is both an alias of attr.social.charisma AND the canonical name of the faction-stat fac.influence; the attribute registers first (first-write-wins) inside both quantity_registry.load() and names.entries(), so the string 'Influence' resolves to the attribute and fac.influence is reachable by NO display string, with NO 'disagreement' possible (the losing candidate is discarded UPSTREAM of resolve()) — disclosed in the docstring and PINNED as a KNOWN LIMITATION (the test asserts the limitation, it does NOT certify the shadowed answer as correct), deferred to the aliases fold-in checkpoint that gives fac.influence a non-colliding pointer (this collision IS the NS2 problem centralization exists to fix); (MED) UnicodeDecodeError (a ValueError, not OSError) escaped the module's 'never raises' contract for every term — fixed with errors='replace' on the read plus except Exception; (MED) `import registry` hard-crashed in a PyYAML-absent context because descriptor_registry.py/quantity_registry.py do a bare `import yaml` (unlike names.py, which guards it) — fixed by guarding the delegate imports so a failed delegate degrades to None per-resolver instead of raising; (MED) a real LIVE disagreement DOES exist in the corpus (Thread Fatigue: names -> thread.thread_fatigue vs quantity_registry -> matched-but-keyless) contradicting the test suite's 'no live disagreement exists' claim — pinned the live case and corrected the docstrings, so the mechanism is now exercised against real data, not only a monkeypatch; (MED) bare structural keys resolve only for attr.* (descriptor_registry.resolve scans attributes only), so fac./set./prac./terr.* keys return None — disclosed, deferred to the fold-in; (MED) the descriptor file was re-parsed on every resolve()/all_known() call — added a module-level cache mirroring the sibling resolvers; (LOW-MED) the `key` field's type flipped between display-string and dotted-key purely by input casing — exposed a uniform `registry_key` dotted structural pointer for every kind (so a name hit like 'Solmund' now carries world.solmund, recoverable through the public API). 25 tests (tests/valoria/test_registry.py). G_pointer resolve-rate meter baseline stays 45.8% — no data has folded yet; the meter climbs in checkpoint 2+ as the registries centralize. Measures/resolves only, never gates.

New sim/cross_scale/echo_transport.py: make_scheduler() + emit_scene_echo() route a resolved personal/scene outcome -> domain_echo.compute_domain_echo (degree-keyed +-2/+-1/0/-1, Sufficient-Scope gated) -> ONE scene.*_resolved Key emitted through the substrate TickScheduler with an OF-7 DEFERRED faction stat_delta apply that lands at the ACTION->ACCOUNTING boundary. Wired into scene_dispatch._resolve_slot (replaces the zoom_out({}) drop) and mc_v18 (world-scoped KeyLog+scheduler; accounting_boundary()+next_tick() per season; CampaignResult.key_log_hash/keys_emitted telemetry). Gated by an ECHO_TRANSPORT flag (default OFF = byte-exact, MB FIELD_MOVEMENT/ED-1089 precedent); the scheduler's PRESENCE on the world is the flag the scene phase reads. VERIFIED: flag-OFF and flag-ON win-share both byte-identical to the F7 seed-42 golden (Crown 12.5 / Varfell 87.5); OF-7 deferral, degree->delta, and byte-identical replay proven directly in sim/tests/test_echo_transport.py (9 cases). SCOPE DISCIPLINE / DEFERRED (nothing silently dropped): (a) the CONTEXT-DERIVATION bridge (deriving scene actors + which faction/stat is at stake from aggregate world-state) stays SC-lane, ED-SC-0006/0007 — so in the LIVE loop every scene still DEFERS and the plumbing is INERT (KeyLog born empty-but-deterministic, sha256 of ''); it is exercised only by the unit test until that bridge lands. (b) parliamentary_vote-into-the-loop (the Hafenmark comeback) is a BALANCE change owned by FA-lane ED-FA-0005 — NOT wired. (c) §5.5 RNG-model fork NOT engaged (domain_echo takes no rng draw). (d) OF-CAP scheduler caps are caller-supplied per the §5.7 ruling (ED-IN-0026) — no fabricated canonical constant. F7's named-zero-assertions (scenes_resolved/insurgencies/npcs) intentionally stay 0 and flip to feature-assertions when the SC bridge lands. Merge ratifies (ED-1094) — the plumbing is complete; nothing held back.

description: valoria-dice-model: added the canonical continuous (Godot-mode) resolver alongside the existing legacy-TTRPG discrete d10 model, per Jordan's confirmation via AskUserQuestion. Prior state: valoria_dice.py implemented only the discrete pool model and the SKILL.md presented it flatly as 'Current standard' with no acknowledgment that params/core.md section Continuous Engine (Decision E, 2026-05-15) designates net ~ Normal(mu*N, sigma*sqrt(N)) as canonical for the videogame/Godot implementation specifically, with the discrete rule demoted to legacy/TTRPG-mode only. Added continuous_outcome_probs(n, tn, ob) and continuous_quick_check(n, tn, ob) to valoria_dice.py -- closed-form via the normal CDF (math.erf, no scipy dependency), continuity-corrected (resolves against x - 0.5 per the ER-2 fix, params/core.md commit a3d3888) so odds track the discrete model at small pools, matching params/core.md's own Degrees of Success thresholds (Overwhelming net >= max(2*Ob,3), Success net >= Ob, Partial 0<net<Ob, Failure net<=0) and supporting fractional Ob (canonical in videogame mode). description: ED-<LANE>-NNNN lane-tagged editorial namespace created (Jordan). Motivated by TWO same-session concurrent-allocation collisions on the flat ED-NNNN sequence within one PR (#58): first ED-1088 collided with an independently-merged mass-battle ED-1088 (LC-8, PR #59), renumbered to ED-1090; then ED-1089/1090 collided AGAIN with three more mass-battle EDs independently landed via PR #62/#65, renumbered to ED-1093/1094 (see ED-1094's own entry for the full incident). The existing references/id_reservations.yaml A-E block scheme only prevents collision through allocation DISCIPLINE (read next_free before allocating, retry on races); two same-session collisions on one active block in a single PR is a real signal that flat-numeric blocks alone do not scale to genuinely concurrent multi-session work on this repo. RULING (Jordan): new EDs use ED-<LANE>-NNNN, a 2-letter lane code + 4-digit zero-padded sequence, making cross-lane collision impossible BY CONSTRUCTION rather than by retryable discipline. Lane roster (9): MB mass battle, PC personal combat, FI field investigation, SC social contest, FA faction actions, WR world, IN infrastructure/cross-cutting, GO godot, SE settlements -- SC (social contest) and PC (personal/scene combat) were deliberately disambiguated after the first draft proposed SC for both; PY (python) was proposed and then dropped as not a real lane (a language, not a subsystem). IMPLEMENTATION: references/id_reservations.yaml gained a lane_ids section (per-lane next_free counters, all starting at 1 except IN which starts at 2 -- this entry is ED-IN-0001, the cutover's own first-ever lane-tagged id, allocated to itself); tools/validate_ed_citations.py's CITE_RE/build_status_map/_walk_entries extended to recognize ED-<LANE>-NNNN alongside flat ED-NNNN (both fold through the same _canon_id normalization, zero-padding-insensitive); tools/currency_consistency_check.py gained check_lane_id_ceilings (per-lane ceiling drift, mirroring the existing flat check_id_ceilings, deliberately independent since the flat ceiling is now frozen); tools/atomizer.py and tools/index_gen.py flagged (not fixed -- low priority, atomizer's archival chunking won't hit lane-tagged volume for a long time; index_gen is already SUPERSEDED/dead) with known-gap comments rather than silent breakage. description: NO SELF-SCHEDULING (CLAUDE.md §11). Jordan directive 2026-07-26 ("I desperately need this check-in every hour thing to go away" / "I don't even need check in triggers, I can just see what's happening by the colours on a session"). MEASURED INCIDENT, window 2026-07-19..26, from the account Routine list: 116 confirmed send_later firings (118 triggers created, all run_once_fired, none pending), concentrated in six chains that polled a single PR for hours — guidebook#19 12 wake-ups/11.2h, ttrpg#237 10/9.3h, ttrpg#236 10/9.1h, guidebook#33 10/9.5h; ~73 chained hours total. 97/118 trigger prompts state CI was already green and 101/118 state the PR was awaiting review/unchanged, so the wake-ups were re-confirming state that only a human could change. PR #237 is the clean case: ten identical hourly re-checks of a 29-check-green PR that then merged when Jordan reached it. COST: a wake-up re-sends the entire conversation; with an EMPTY conversation that is still CLAUDE.md (48,612 chars ~ 12,153 tok) + system prompt/tool schemas (~10k) + SessionStart banner (~1k) ~ 23.2k tok, so 116 firings ~ 2.7M tokens as an ARITHMETIC FLOOR (real sessions were mid-PR carrying far more — the true figure is a multiple). Added context per wake-up is separate and additive: one get_check_runs on this repo measures 9.4KB ~ 2.4k tok. Median wake-to-wake gap 61.9 min with 59/75 gaps in the 60-70 min band — the re-arm is delay=1h measured from the END of the previous turn, so every gap overshoots the 1h prompt-cache TTL by 2-3 min and most re-sends were UNCACHED (near the worst reachable interval). FIX (enforced, not conventional, per §0.1 point 5 — one owner + a guard that fails on recurrence): .claude/settings.json permissions.deny is the single owner, blocking send_later (the measured mechanism), create_trigger (its underlying Routine API, i.e. the route-around), ScheduleWakeup and CronCreate (/loop pacing + fixed-interval), each across all three claude-code-remote server-name spellings since a deny rule matches the fully-qualified tool name. tools/ci_hooks_verifier.py Check 6 (BLOCKING job 'Enforcement Architecture Intact') fails if any primitive is dropped or if §11 goes missing. FALSIFIER (§0.1 point 3): tests/valoria/test_no_polling_triggers.py — MUTATION-VERIFIED, each of the four primitives deleted in turn, every deletion caught by both the test and the CI job (send_later 2 failed, create_trigger 2 failed, ScheduleWakeup 1 failed, CronCreate 1 failed; verifier exit 1 in all four). LIMIT OF THE GUARD, stated plainly: no test can observe a hosted session actually calling the tool — it pins the artifacts and the roster, so a NEW self-scheduling primitive would pass until added to REQUIRED_DENY in both files. GitHub webhook delivery of real PR activity (<github-webhook-activity> CI failures / review comments) is push-based and unaffected — nothing about this rule reduces responsiveness to events that actually happened. ALSO DONE: deleted the dormant hourly cron Routine 'Coverage-completion loop (guidebook)' (8 * * * *, created 2026-07-21T19:27Z, last_fired 2026-07-24T14:03Z) — the adjacent non-send_later poller surfaced by the same sweep.

(1) on_exceed vocabulary: tools/compliance_check.py graded severity inline as "warn if startswith('flag') else error", so warn_only (12 files) and chunk_by_quarter (a split strategy, not a severity) had NEVER worked -- both silently blocking. Replaced with a CLOSED vocabulary single-owned by _on_exceed_severity(); an unimplemented token now raises UnknownOnExceedToken naming the token and the declaring file instead of defaulting to a blocking error. Found while fixing it: the CI-mode path (--check-only --repo-state) carried its OWN divergent copy that never honoured 'skip', so an explicitly-exempted file over cap graded as a blocking error there while exempt on the other path -- both sites now route through the owner. NOTE the first mutation attempt was INVALID (it patched a neighbouring family's artifact_paths) and produced a false PASS -- recorded because a mutation check that cannot reach its target is itself the 0.1 #2 defect. title: M1 program scaffolding: scope ratchet, season acceptance gate, dashboard program panel — decision policy HELD for Jordan
description: Scaffolding for the M1 program ('one playable season'), which has sat at 0/7 junctures while the corpus grew, with no surface reporting that as a program signal. THREE ARTIFACTS LANDED. (1) SCOPE RATCHET - tools/scope_ratchet.py + registers/scope_baseline.yaml, five measured ceilings (ed.open 215, ed.needs_jordan 86, audit.files 1264, tracked.files 3103, proposals.open 20). Deliberately a SEPARATE instrument from review_baseline.yaml: every review_core signal is a quality signal, and scope growth is not a quality regression, so the existing ratchet is structurally blind to it. Carries a RAISE GUARD - --seed lowers freely (banking a shrink) and REFUSES to raise without --allow-raise, because a --seed that raises on every run is a mirror, not a ratchet; raising is an ED-1094 act. (2) ACCEPTANCE GATE - tools/m1_acceptance.py turns 'fully simulatable season' from an unbounded phrase into five falsifiable rows. FOUR OF FIVE REPORT 'blocked' AND NAME WHAT UNBLOCKS THEM rather than guessing a value: a gate reporting readiness it has not measured is the ED-MB-0042 confound rebuilt as infrastructure. Row 3 (key closure) is exact-static, reading the emits/consumes + terminal flags already in module_contracts.yaml - MEASURED 47 emitted, 0 declared terminal, 2 orphaned (env.crisis, mechanical.season_change), a real finding. (3) DASHBOARD PANEL - build_program/renderProgram, the first card that answers 'is the goal moving?' rather than 'what is the state of the corpus?'; composes the two tools by import and adds no arithmetic of its own. TWO SELF-CAUGHT DEFECTS, both from running rather than reading: the acceptance gate's first key-closure implementation guessed the contract field names and reported '0 orphaned of 0 emitted' - a vacuous pass of exactly the class ci_vacuous_assertion_check (ED-IN-0098) landed to catch; and the hand-transcribed baselines were stale within twenty minutes (214->215, 3090->3103) because three PRs merged mid-session, which is why seeding is now an operation (--seed) rather than a number someone typed. The ratchet then caught its own author: a proposals/ doc for this program would have pushed proposals.open 20->21 and regressed the ceiling on its own introducing commit, so no such doc was written and the POINTER carries the scope instead. MEASURED-BY: tools/scope_ratchet.py --summary reproduces every ceiling and the M1 health number; tools/m1_acceptance.py --summary reproduces the acceptance rows including the 47 emitted / 0 declared-terminal / 2 orphaned key census. Both read the working tree on every run and cache nothing, so a disputed number is re-derivable by running them rather than by trusting this entry. RATIFIED ON MERGE 2026-07-31 (PR #277). EFFECTIVENESS WIRING added in the same pass: an adversarial critic found the ratchet had NO executing caller except the test suite, i.e. the instrument was inert. It is now a REPORT-ONLY entry in tools/valoria_local.py's check table — which runs both pre-commit AND in CI's generation-consistency-check job — and is registered in references/ci_checks_registry.yaml. Deliberately NOT a new CI job: this repo has 34 and adding a 35th to report one number would be the very defect the instrument measures. Report-only is load-bearing, not timidity: an earlier version asserted its --check inside the BLOCKING pytest suite at zero headroom, which would have broken the build for the next author to file an ED. Promotion to blocking is a Jordan call with a loud ED-1094 call-out. SHIPPING GATE PARALLELISED: unit-tests 387s -> 180.7s in CI (2.15x; 3.02x locally), with failure/pass/skip counts byte-identical (10/1282/21 both sides). `-n auto` changes WHERE tests run, never WHICH — pytest.ini's ONE RULE forbids a -m filter here as a shipping-gate coverage cut, and that rule was read BEFORE building, which is what stopped this session shipping a coverage cut labelled as a speedup.

Nothing in this PR adopts a precedence order among canon / historical precedent / physical factuality, an operational test for 'emergent', or a deliberate-fantasy exception clause. Those are Jordan's to author (agents may draft for correction); the scaffolding here measures and reports and rules nothing. Rationale: the queue is evidence-rich and answer-poor - 83 of 85 needs_jordan items carry a source pointer and only 10 carry a proposed answer - so a stated policy is what lets most of them resolve without Jordan, and deriving against an UNSTATED precedence order would manufacture confident wrong answers wearing citations.

title: Age-weight the scope ratchet's ledger signals — the metric punished FILING, not rot
description: Closes the KNOWN METRIC FLAW filed with ED-IN-0112 and deliberately left unfixed there. `ed.open` and `ed.needs_jordan` were raw censuses, so they conflated WORK OPENED with WORK NOT CLOSED: appending a ledger row — the behaviour CLAUDE.md SS2 expects of substantively every PR — regressed the ceiling by one. A gate that fires on the correct action is a gate that gets ignored, and the baseline file predicted exactly that while shipping it anyway. I then compounded it by calling the flaw 'not load-bearing on M1', correcting myself that it IS load-bearing precisely during the queue drain, and still not fixing it. FIX: both signals are now AGE-WEIGHTED at STALE_DAYS=30. `ed.stale` counts open items older than 30 days; `ed.needs_jordan_stale` the same for the bottleneck subset. MEASURED on the 2026-07-31 tree: 213 open -> 76 stale (137 aged <=30d, 61 aged 31-60d, 11 aged >60d, 4 undated); 94 needs_jordan -> 21 stale. Targets re-derived rather than carried over (20 and 3, the latter following the measured ~1-in-6 genuine-taste share applied to the STALE subset rather than the whole queue). UNDATED COUNTS AS STALE (4 rows). An entry with no parseable date cannot be SHOWN to be fresh, and treating unknown age as zero is the same 'absence of evidence reads as a pass' defect this module already rejects for unmeasurable signals. SINGLE-OWNER EXTENSION, NOT A SECOND READER: obs_core.read_ledger_entries dropped `date` during normalisation, so age was unavailable to every consumer. Rather than parse dates separately in scope_ratchet — which would have recreated the exact second-ledger-reader defect ED-IN-0112's adversarial pass had just removed — obs_core now carries a normalised `date` (YYYY-MM-DD prefix, None when absent/unparseable so a consumer must decide explicitly). Every other consumer gains age for free. PINNED: a test that constructs BOTH cases and requires they differ — filing a fresh item must not move the stale count, a second rotted item must — plus one asserting an undated open row counts as stale. Neither can pass if the metric reverts to a raw census.

title: run.dispute() callers passed four keys the harness never reads — every dispute was keyed '?'
description: Closes the HARNESS DEFECT filed as an ED-IN-0087 residual after the live W4 run. The obvious repair was to repoint it at systems/. That would have been wrong twice: its advice ('extract prose to *_infill.md') and its threshold (400 lines) both encode the index+infill convention CLAUDE.md S4 RETIRED on 2026-07-26, so repointing as-is emits 29 warnings recommending an abandoned practice; and the rule is not its own — tools/compliance_check.py reads references/atomization_rules.yaml (the single owner of the 15,000-token cap) and ALREADY reports every oversized systems/ doc. (2) COMBAT test_status — LANE-QUALIFIED, per Jordan's 'maybe you can implement PC as part of your nomenclature'. Every validated_* value encoded a MONTE-CARLO SAMPLE SIZE, which assumes the only way to validate a mechanic is to run it N times. Personal combat was never validated that way: its engine was ratified (ED-900/904) and its Godot slice checked for key-log PARITY against the Python oracle (2026-06-23). So `combat` carried a bare `validated` matching no enum value, and the schema validator errored on it every run — invisible while mechanics_index_gen was fataling out on a retired root marker. New value `validated_pc` names the LANE and its standard, using the ED-<LANE> codes already canonical in S3/S4. Add a sibling only when a lane has a standard to point at. mechanics_index_gen now reports 0 errors / 0 warnings (was 3 errors + 39 warnings when revived).

(3) THE SEVEN NEVER-AUTHORED canon_authoring_target ROWS — RESOLVED BY DERIVATION, NOT BY DISCRETION. They carried designs/ prefixes for a retired tree, and I filed them as a subsystem-lane design call. That framing was wrong: RULED S2a binds one subsystem = one folder = one ID lane, and each mechanic's sim_module ALREADY lives in a subsystem package, so the doc's home follows mechanically. varfell_territorial_acquisition / infrastructure_reclamation / home_sanctuary_t9 / crown_treaty -> systems/factions/ (FA); altonian_reinforcements / hafenmark_equipment -> systems/mass_battle/ (MB); restoration_movement -> systems/world/ (WR, scale world/emergent). Each row now states NOT YET AUTHORED, the pending pass, the lane, and the sim module the home was derived from. (4) EXECUTIVE-SUMMARY DRIFT (flagged by the PR #245 session, unfixed there). The handoff summary is AUTHORED not generated — deliberately, because a generated summary is a table of contents. The cost is that it decays undetectably: items close, new ones land, and the paragraph a reader trusts most quietly stops describing the file under it. It now carries two RECOMPUTABLE facts — the live-item count and the newest item's date — and handoff_atomize.summary_drift() reports when either diverges, plus when a summary asserts nothing checkable at all (which cannot drift only because it never said anything). Human judgement kept, decay made observable. Report-only: it runs inside a tool an author invokes, never a commit gate.

description:
CURRENT.md's STALENESS STAMP NO LONGER TRIPS ON APPARATUS. The stamp answers one question — has a canonical head moved since CURRENT.md was last reconciled? — but it was asked of every path CURRENT.md names, and 15 of those 77 are tools/ or tests/. Editing a validator or a unit test cannot stale a canon index, yet it tripped the gate, and the only way to clear it was a reflex date bump that reconciled nothing. This session paid that toll twice.

MEASURED, AND THE FILED CLAIM WAS OVERSTATED. The report that prompted this said the stamp trips on 'essentially every infrastructure PR'. History says a quarter, not nearly all: over the 57 commits since 2026-06-28, 51 would trip the stamp, and 12 of those (24%) touched a tracked tools/ or tests/ path and NO canonical head at all. The honest counter-number is that 36 more trip via a canonical head TOO, so this narrows the noise rather than eliminating the check. Both figures argue for the same change, which is exactly why the stronger one had to be checked rather than adopted — S0.1 point 4: a number without a control is not a measurement in either direction, and a favourable framing is not a reason to skip the control.

The EXISTENCE half — check_current_paths_exist — is deliberately left covering every path including tools/ and tests/, because CURRENT.md naming a deleted validator is real drift and is precisely the rot ED-IN-0087 spent its time on. One question narrowed, the other untouched.

system: infrastructure / cross-cutting (workflow apparatus — verification of a shipped assumption)
description:
P4's LOAD-BEARING ASSUMPTION VERIFIED, having shipped unverified in ED-IN-0087 and been tagged [PART] under adversarial review. THE CLAIM: every critic stage in .claude/wf_*.js passes BOTH `agentType: 'valoria-critic'` (frontmatter `tools: Read, Grep, Glob`) AND a `schema`. A schema forces a StructuredOutput TOOL call. If the frontmatter list excluded that injected tool, all six critic stages would return null — and, worse, the harness's own `.catch(() => null)` + `.filter(Boolean)` pattern would have HIDDEN that failure until the run.attempt() fix landed.

METHOD — a controlled experiment, not a smoke test (S0.1 point 4). Three agents, sonnet/low: (1) the restricted critic reads a file and reports its own tool list through a schema; (2) an UNRESTRICTED CONTROL runs the byte-identical prompt and schema, so a null from arm 1 could be attributed to the agentType rather than to a bad prompt or schema; (3) the restricted critic is asked to create /tmp/valoria_critic_write_probe.txt, with the target confirmed ABSENT beforehand so a success could not be a pre-existing file.

RESULT — the assumption HOLDS, and the evidence is direct rather than inferential. The restricted agent reported its own tools as [Read, Grep, Glob, StructuredOutput]: the schema tool is injected ON TOP of the frontmatter list, which is exactly the composition in question. The control reported 20+ tools including Write, Edit and Bash, proving the restriction is real and that the prompt/schema pair was never the variable. Both arms returned validated objects; the workflow journal records 0 null results across all 3 agents. The write probe returned succeeded=false, and — because an agent asserting it cannot write is not proof it cannot — the filesystem was checked independently: no file was created.

COST: 3 agents, 114,621 subagent tokens, 15.1s. Cheap enough that shipping the assumption unverified was never justified by cost; it was justified by nothing.

RECORDED IN ALL THREE PLACES THAT CARRIED THE ASSUMPTION — .claude/agents/valoria-critic.md (which previously stated the restriction as fact), tools/ci_wf_harness_check.py's docstring (which enforces the routing), and HANDOFF_IN.md (whose [PART] tag now names only the one remaining residual: hSameFinding's containment thresholds are still calibrated on wording rather than measured against a live multi-lens run). MEASURED-BY: tools/ci_wf_harness_check.py

title: The blocking anti-fabrication gate matched 0 of 117 live oracle files — and was a wall on the rest
description: CLAUDE.md §7 leans on tools/ci_sim_fabrication_check.py as the guard on the 1:1 Python reference the Godot port validates against. MEASURED 2026-08-01: is_sim_file() matched 0 of 117 .py files under engine/** and systems/*/sim/**, and the gate printed '[SIM-FABRICATION OK] no changed sim .py files — nothing to check.' over the entire oracle. The predicate asked whether the BASENAME contains 'sim' — a sound proxy while the oracle lived under sim/, where every path did. sim/ was retired 2026-07-21 and its contents distributed to engine/ and systems/<subsystem>/sim/, where no basename contains 'sim' (massbattle.py, mc_v18.py, resolver.py). §0.1 point-5 signature: correct when written, broken by a move elsewhere. It also ignored ci_common.sim_reference_prefixes(), the declared ONE OWNER (OI-53a/ED-IN-0097), while importing ci_common for everything else. SECOND DEFECT, found only by measuring the fix before shipping it: violations were computed over the WHOLE FILE while 'added' merely selected which files to scan. Repairing the predicate alone would have dragged 642 pre-existing uncited constants across 47 oracle files into a BLOCKING gate, walling off the MB and PC lanes — the exact cost ED-IN-0097's cap raise paid. The same measurement showed the whole-file scan was never viable even in its original scope: tests/sim carries 2,283 uncited constants across 88 files, so any changeset touching one met a blocking gate with hundreds of violations. The gate was therefore blind on one side and impassable on the other, and had never functioned as designed. FIX: is_sim_file() now derives its roots from ci_common.sim_reference_prefixes() (engine/tests/ excluded deliberately — gating a regression suite's fixture constants would demand ledger citations for arbitrary seeds); violations are scoped to lines the changeset ADDED, which is what the gate's own pure-rename exemption already reasons toward ('this gate catches NEWLY-fabricated constants') without applying it. Pre-existing debt is never dropped silently: the carried count prints on EVERY run, pass or fail, and --full lists it for a deliberate burn-down. NOT DONE, recorded not silently skipped: the 642 + 2,283 pre-existing uncited constants are a real backlog this change makes visible and does not burn down. title: A gate blind for 14 days, a dashboard surface blind for 17, and the pattern guard that should have been written on 2026-08-01
description: THE PATTERN, not the instances: a tool declares a repo-relative path as a module-level constant; a restructure moves the target; the read silently yields nothing (os.walk and glob on a missing directory return empty rather than raising) and the tool reports clean over an unscanned input. This is the CLAUDE.md §0.1 point-5 signature verbatim — the code was correct when written and broke because something else changed — and it had already been fixed ONCE as a one-off the previous day (canon_coverage_check repointed designs/ -> systems/ on 2026-08-01, after 13 days reporting 0 findings against a 130-path registry under --strict) WITHOUT a guard. Two repoints and no guard is the pattern going unlearned, so this entry's deliverable is the guard; the instances below are what it caught. (1) ci_formula_prose_check.DEFAULT_CENSUS pointed at designs/audit/2026-07-08-.../quantity_census.yaml. The census moved with the whole designs/audit/ corpus on 2026-07-19 (ED-IN-0071 P4/P5). load_census() returned [] and the CI report rendered '_No formula prose-drift found in scope._' for 14 days. Repointed: 88 census rows scanned, 49 formula-bearing, 14 CENSUS_DRIFT findings surfaced. The tool is report-only so this changes no CI verdict — it changes CI from asserting an unmeasured zero to reporting a measured 14. load_census() now returns (rows, problem) because its three failure modes (no pyyaml / missing file / parse error) were INDISTINGUISHABLE downstream from a genuinely empty census, and the report rendered all four identically; 'cannot measure' and 'measured zero' now render differently, which is the condition that would have made the 14-day blindness self-announcing (§0.1 point 4). (2) dashboard_data.HANDOFFS_DIR = 'handoffs'. The lane handoffs moved to registers/handoffs/ on 2026-07-16 (ED-IN-0071 P0b). os.path.isdir() was False, the listdir loop never ran, and _handoff_files() returned root HANDOFF.md alone for 17 days. Repointed and MEASURED against the blind value as a control: files 1 -> 11, build_needs_decision() items 2 -> 7 — five decision markers across the FA/IN/PC/SC lanes were absent from the published dashboard. (3) Two dead paths stamped into GENERATED artifacts (build_proposals.RANKED_QUEUE, build_lexicon's s_st provenance label) — both emitted a designs/ citation that no longer resolves; build_lexicon's actual READ already used the live path, so only the citation was dead. build_proposals' dead (REPO/'designs').rglob was removed rather than repointed: designs/ is retired and must not be recreated (CLAUDE.md §3), so the glob was dead weight that would have silently resurrected a scan of a forbidden tree. DELIBERATELY NOT FIXED: compliance_check.find_index_for's designs/ prefix (behind the dead orchestrator-era _github_ops path, §8) and the 'designs'/'sim' entries in ci_program_claim_check.TREES / ci_claude_workflow_paths.TREES — those are RECOGNIZER tokens that must keep naming retired trees so dead paths can be identified and reported. Prose and docstring citations of designs/ were left alone throughout: CLAUDE.md §3 says they resolve via references/restructure_ledger.md's alias map. MEASURED-BY: tests/valoria/test_tool_input_paths_resolve.py
measured_by: tests/valoria/test_tool_input_paths_resolve.py — an AST scan of every module-level path constant in tools/**/*.py (69 cases, 1 documented output exemption). AST rather than grep is load-bearing: comments and docstrings are not in the parsed statement tree, so the dozens of legitimate designs/ prose citations are excluded BY CONSTRUCTION rather than by a filter. The invariant is direction-free ('a declared input path must exist') rather than a blocklist of retired tree names, which would already be obsolete when written. MUTATION-VERIFIED, 9/9 mutants killed — and two of them SURVIVED the first draft, which is the reason the file is shaped as it is: (a) an early '/'-separator requirement excluded single-segment constants, i.e. it missed canon_coverage_check's DESIGNS_DIR = os.path.join(_REPO_ROOT, 'designs'), THE VERY DEFECT THE GUARD IS NAMED AFTER; measured that admitting them adds 5 constants, all real, all resolving, zero false positives. (b) a value-based TREES head-gate cannot see a constant repointed to a typo (AUDIT_DIR = 'audits'), so a name-based discriminator (*_DIR/_PATH/_GLOB/_FILE/_ROOT) was added — naming is the more reliable signal precisely because it survives the value going wrong. (c) the anti-vacuity floor was raised and split PER SHAPE after crippling one _literal_path branch still left 32 constants, comfortably over the original floor of 20 — a total-count floor cannot see half a scan die. The guard found instance (2) itself, unprompted. title: Fork direction INVERTED (keep main, evacuate prose); J1 reinterpreted; eight held C-items ruled, two struck as non-decisions
description: THE DIRECTION IS INVERTED (Jordan, 2026-08-04). Every prior artifact assumed the fork receives the CODE and prose is left behind. Jordan: 'our fork is going to hold all the outdated largely-prose work that contaminates our code-based work' and 'if we keep MAIN for our actual ongoing work, it's a lot cleaner going forward than with a fork'. So: THIS repo is the code-first go-forward repo; the fork/archive receives the outdated prose. This is the EVACUATE arm of audit/2026-08-03-session-oddities.md section M, now ruled. (1) J1 REGISTERED REINTERPRETED, NOT VERBATIM. J1 ruled 'main does NOT keep moving after the fork' when 'the fork' meant an extracted code repo. Under the inversion the referents swap: the ARCHIVE freezes at the evacuation tag; main continues. Registering the literal wording would have frozen the go-forward repo. The E1 objection (build_fork.py is a one-way rmtree build that would clobber fork-side commits) stays dissolved, because nothing is rebuilt from main into the archive. (2) THE PROSE RULE, three-way and testable. Prose with NO code pair STAYS and is authoritative -- it IS the spec (canon/ P-01..P-14; the 14 `godot: no-oracle` module specs, consistent with the fork plan's own section 4: 'the prose is the only spec that exists... demoted from runtime authority, not from the repo'). Prose WITH a code pair STAYS as information only; code wins (principle 7 / ED-1050). Prose that is NEITHER evacuates: session audits, process ledgers, arcs/, workplans/, superseded proposals. CONSEQUENCE: engine/params/ has code pairs, so it is information-only and STAYS demoted rather than being deleted -- J11's premise ('the fork's biggest deletion') dissolves, and with it the risk of orphaning ~50 provenance citations that kept code (including the canon MB engine's core arithmetic at orchestration.py:2438,:2546,:2553) makes into those tables. Measured, with a positive control that passes: zero runtime readers of engine/params in engine/ or systems/; the same method finds the real path constructions for key_type_registry_v30.md at echo_transport.py:62 and build_graph.py:50. Two earlier attempts at that measurement FAILED their positive control and were discarded rather than reported. (3) SECTION M'S MECHANISM IS UNSAFE AS WRITTEN and must not be executed. 'git rm everything that is not in CARRY' assumes CARRY union LEAVE partitions the tree. It does not. The neither-set includes .github/, .githooks/, .claude/, tools/, tests/valoria/, most of references/, research/, skills/, and the root files CLAUDE.md / CURRENT.md / HANDOFF.md. Under extract the neither-set defaults to left-behind; under evacuate the same command DELETES it -- i.e. the entire enforcement tier (CLAUDE.md section 8), the shipping gate, and the session protocol. LEAVE also conflates two categories that only extraction merges: prose contamination (audit/, arcs/, most proposals/) versus SOURCE-REPO INFRASTRUCTURE, where build_fork.py's own rationales are extraction-only -- tools/ 'the fork re-derives what it needs' and tests/valoria/ 'engine/tests comes instead'. Under keep-main tests/valoria/ is the shipping gate AND the home of the fork plan's own falsifiers (test_faction_l_reconstruction, test_key_graph, test_execution_map, test_public_governance_transfer_key). The keep-set must therefore be AUTHORED FRESH, not run backwards. (4) THE EIGHT HELD C-ITEMS, RULED (Jordan, 2026-08-04). C1 -- personal combat is triggered by field investigation, mass battle, AND scene contest, and can also be invoked directly: four entry points, not the single escalation hook the docket offered; engine/cross_scale/combat_bridge.py is the already-built seam (OI-01). C2 -- mass battle occurs ON A MAP; the loser of the scene is whoever loses more units or has their settlement captured (registered against the degree blocker in ED-MB-0064). C3 -- engine_clock stands; it is the season counter PLUS the accounting boundary (TickScheduler, engine/substrate/keys.py:404, whose docstring already calls itself 'the engine_clock-shaped emission seam'), and the cheap close is to point its `doc: null` at the CANONICAL systems/_architecture/propagation_spec_v1.md rather than author a new spine (ED-1051). C4 -- TEN attributes: 3/3/3 plus Spirit. Jordan flagged this as NOT fully settled, so the Character dataclass keeps attributes as a descriptor_registry-keyed dict; the roster stays data and the count stays reversible. C5 -- STRUCK, not a decision (see 5). C6 -- NO new da.territorial_transfer key type: the owner of territory is already keyed (target_territory_id, systems/_architecture/key_type_registry_v30.md:200; falsifier tests/valoria/test_public_governance_transfer_key.py). C7 -- STRUCK, not a decision (see 5). C8 -- Church Influence is a GLOBAL peninsula-wide tracker that gates behaviours and actions (e.g. the mass-seizure attempt); territorial_piety is a per-territory stat for how religious that territory is, and it FEEDS CI. They were never one contested scalar, so B5's 'contested CI scalar' was a category error, not a single-owner defect. (5) TWO HELD ITEMS WERE NEVER DECISIONS, and both arose the same way -- an absence read as a prohibition. C7 asked 'is a one-turn rout with an untouched winner correct?' when Jordan had ALREADY ruled it a real defect (F1-class) that same day: audit/2026-08-03-session-oddities.md:55 (D1). The plan re-opened it at proposals/valoria_fork_plan_of_record_v1.md:342-344 ('Only Jordan can answer that') and filed it at :413. It is also incoherent against canon: PP-233 'Damage is simultaneous' is implemented and cited throughout tests/sim/mass_battle/orchestration.py (:1834, :1839, :2053, :2056, :2372, :2698; damage recorded Phase 2, applied Phase 6 Step 1 at :1503/:1983), so a winner taking ZERO losses in 42/60 battles is a damage-path defect, not a balance opinion. J9 (is the rout firing before damage lands, and does one fix green all nine red MB tests?) is the live thread. C5 read ED-1006's finding -- 'scale_transitions SS3 has NO top-down Key-delivery rule (provincial/peninsula -> personal/scene/settlement all uncovered)' -- as a gate. It is a recorded GAP. title: build_fork.py scanned clean over an empty tree: --verify-only could not run as documented, and printed a green line over zero files
description: THE DEFECT. `tools/build_fork.py --out <fresh-dir> --verify-only` skips assemble() (:324), so the output tree never exists. os.walk on a nonexistent path YIELDS NOTHING rather than raising, so the escape scan printed 'no path literal reaches an uncarried tree' over ZERO files -- textually identical to the clean result, carrying none of its meaning -- and the run then died at the FORK_MANIFEST.json write (:399) with a bare FileNotFoundError. Both halves were wrong: a green line that meant nothing, then an illegible failure. This is the gate-reporting-clean-over-nothing class (#283/#284) reproduced inside the tool the fork plan names as its STEP 1. BLAST RADIUS ON THE PLAN, which is why this is not cosmetic: the command appears as step 1 in proposals/valoria_fork_plan_of_record_v1.md:64 and registers/handoffs/HANDOFF_IN.md:40, and the plan's section 11 item 4 names '--verify-only on a clean checkout' as the SETTLING MEASUREMENT for its own 'the carry list may be stale' risk. On a clean checkout there is no assembled tree, so that measurement could never have run. A falsifier that cannot execute is not a falsifier. SCOPE CORRECTION, recorded because the first report of this defect overstated it: only the ESCAPE scan was vacuous. contract_coverage() takes NO argument (:195) and reads the SOURCE repo's module_contracts.yaml (:216) against the CARRY constant -- it is a source-side static check, valid with or without an output tree. And the run died non-zero rather than exiting green, so this is a LESSER class than #283's silently-clean gates: misleading stdout plus a bad crash. Corrected by an independent read-only critic pass. THE FIX -- the class, not the crash. New single owner `_scanned_py(out)` answers 'which .py files does a tree-scan see' and REFUSES to return an empty list: it raises EmptyScanError on a missing directory or one with no Python. Both scanners (escapes, classify) route their file discovery through it, so the guard is on the path rather than merely available; main() checks it before printing anything and exits 2 with a message that says what to do. REJECTED ALTERNATIVE: having --verify-only assemble into a temp dir. That silently verifies a DIFFERENT tree than the one the caller named and collapses the two documented modes (:22-24) into one. --verify-only re-verifies an EXISTING assembled tree; if there isn't one, say so. FALSIFIER (CLAUDE.md 0.1 point 3): tests/valoria/test_build_fork_scan_guard.py, 7 tests, MUTATION-VERIFIED -- 4 of 4 planted mutants killed. (M1) guard returns [] instead of raising on a missing dir -> 4 failed. (M2) guard raises UNCONDITIONALLY -> 2 failed, caught by test_the_guard_itself_can_fail, the positive control that exists precisely so an always-raising guard cannot make this file vacuously green. (M3) escapes() bypasses the guard with a raw glob -> 1 failed. (M4) __pycache__ no longer excluded -> 1 failed. build_fork.py restored byte-exact after the mutation run (cmp clean) and the control re-run is 7 passed. The tests are UNIT-LEVEL by construction: tests/valoria is a blocking CI job, so nothing here calls assemble() (copies the tree) or verify_runs() (spawns a seeded campaign subprocess). BEHAVIOUR CONFIRMED BOTH WAYS by execution, not inference: fresh dir -> '[FORK] CANNOT VERIFY: ... does not exist. --verify-only re-verifies an ALREADY-ASSEMBLED tree', exit 2, and NO clean-scan line printed; already-built tree -> unchanged, exit 0, RUNS STANDALONE with the same hash c2da472354077b9c. title: workplans/ kept, audit window widened to all of July, and the criterion that makes context safe to keep is a status marker, not recency
description: Jordan, 2026-08-04: 'we still need workplans as a directory and we need to retain most recent plans probably. we need some semblance of context for our work rather than 100% new. or is that a bad idea due to baggage?' RULED: workplans/ is KEPT (13 files -- valoria_master_workplan_v6.md, workplan_v6_progress.yaml which the SessionStart banner reads, a README, and 10 POINTER stubs per ED-IN-0103). This also RESOLVES the coupling flagged in ED-IN-0128: dashboard/ was kept while its input workplans/ was evacuating, which would have left dashboard_data.py and workplan_status.py reading missing files. Both are now kept; the coupling is closed rather than deferred. THE ANSWER TO 'IS IT BAGGAGE', which is a design finding and not a preference. Measured on this session's own errors: EVERY stale-material defect corrected today came from RECENT material, not old material -- ci_track.py's DRIFT note (cited a path retired 2026-07-21, read as current by two readers), build_execution_map.py's '3 of 27' (retracted the day before), build_fork.py's canon assertion, the plan's three false 'Prepared how' rows (written the same week), HANDOFF_IN's 'UNRESOLVED' block (contradicted by a ruling in the same file). Not one was an April document. Nobody mistakes a 2026-04 session record for current state; the poison is material that is recent AND whose status cannot be read at a glance. SO THE CRITERION IS A STATUS MARKER, NOT AGE. Context that carries its own status is safe to keep at any size: workplans/ has a progress board and pointer stubs, CURRENT.md is a stamp chain, HANDOFF_<LANE>.md carries [OPEN]/[PART]/[DONE] tags (ED-IN-0086). Context that does not is unsafe at any age. MEASURED, and this is where the residual risk actually sits: of the 71 in-window audit .md files the two-week rule KEEPS, only 15 carry a '## Status:' line -- 56 are undated present-tense prose snapshots, which is precisely the shape that produced today's errors. The two-week window bounds the exposure but does not remove it. NOT ACTED ON, filed: requiring kept audit .md to carry a status line (or a superseded-by pointer) would close the residual. ci_generation_consistency.py already enforces '## Status:' on governed files; audits are not in its census. That is a gate widening, not a deletion, and it belongs with the audit slice rather than here. MEASURED-BY: tools/evacuation_plan.py -- `--check` reproduces the partition after the flip (3148 tracked -> 1164 keep / 6 relocate / 1978 evacuate; evacuating roots 6 -> 5, workplans removed). MEASURED-BY: tests/valoria/test_evacuation_plan.py -- 24 tests green post-flip. AUDIT WINDOW WIDENED (Jordan, 2026-08-04): 'probably keep audits from july overall'. AUDIT_CUTOFF 2026-07-21 -> 2026-07-01. Effect: R-AUDIT-RECENT 148 -> 675, R-AUDIT-STALE 1087 -> 560; partition 1164/6/1978 -> 1691/6/1451. July is the period the current architecture was built in, so this buys continuity of reasoning rather than volume. Note the residual risk scales with it: the status-marker census above was 15 of 71 in-window files; the window is now ~4.5x larger, so the proportion of unmarked present-tense prose in the kept set grows. The cheap mitigation (require a status line on kept audits) moves from optional to advisable. test_audit_cutoff_boundary was rewritten to derive its boundary from AUDIT_CUTOFF instead of hardcoding 2026-07-20, so moving the cutoff re-aims the test rather than silently falsifying it -- the old form would have passed while testing nothing.

title: The reader scan could not see split paths — a kept tool's oracle was in the evacuate set
description: FOUND BY an independent read-only Fable-5 adversarial audit, not by the author. THE CASUALTY. audit/2026-06-03-contest-groundup/engine.py was classified EVACUATE by R-AUDIT-STALE. Kept tools/gen_sigma_parity_goldens.py:96 LOADS IT BY PATH to regenerate the committed golden engine/tests/goldens/sigma_leverage_parity.json, and kept CI test engine/tests/test_sigma_leverage_parity.py:115 asserts on it (by_oracle['groundup'] >= 259). Evacuating it leaves a committed generated table with NO SOURCE -- a frozen artifact that can never be re-derived, the exact stale-artifact hazard this programme keeps closing. It does NOT relocate: gen_sigma's docstring :11-12 says both parity oracles are frozen provenance that must stay put, and that generator exists precisely to INVERT the coupling (oracle stays, test reads a table). Fixed by R-PARITY-GROUNDUP, a file-level keep. THE CLASS, which matters far more than the instance. readers() greps for the literal 'audit/'. gen_sigma builds its path as os.path.join(REPO_ROOT, 'audit', '2026-06-03-contest-groundup', 'engine.py') -- SEGMENTS, no such substring. A substring scan CANNOT see a split path; not did not, cannot. So the per-slice 'blocking readers' counts that were meant to sequence a safe deletion were structurally blind to an entire construction idiom. Added joined_path_readers(): AST-walks every kept .py, reconstructs os.path.join / Path() / '/'-chain calls from their CONSTANT segments (variables skipped, never guessed -- guessing is the fabrication this repo forbids), and tests the rebuilt path against the evacuate roots. IT IMMEDIATELY FOUND 45 READERS THE SUBSTRING SCAN MISSED, including three genuine breakages beyond the oracle: tests/valoria/test_gen_audit.py -> deprecated/archives, tools/currency_consistency_check.py -> deprecated/skills, and tools/sim_harness/adapters/pr119_governance/pr119_structural_gaps.py -> tests/sim/settlement_mgmt_stress_01. It also surfaced ~20 in-window audit probes under audit/2026-07-22-mass-battle-stress-test/ that import from tests/sim -- i.e. the July cutoff keeps files whose dependency evacuates. That coupling is now visible instead of latent. FALSIFIER: three new tests. test_split_path_scan_finds_what_substring_scan_cannot pins the scan against the live tree; test_the_split_scan_can_fail is the positive control (a PLANTED os.path.join into deprecated/ must be reported, so an always-empty scanner cannot pass); test_the_parity_oracle_is_not_evacuated is the regression pin for the casualty itself. 27 tests green. ALSO REFUTED FROM THE SAME AUDIT, recorded because an audit's own claims need checking: it reported id_reservations.yaml next_free NOT bumped past ED-IN-0128. It was -- the file reads 130. The auditor read a mid-session snapshot. MEASURED-BY: tools/evacuation_plan.py -- the report now prints a SPLIT-PATH section per slice; partition 3148 -> 1700 keep / 6 relocate / 1442 evacuate. title: The evacuation would have broken the blocking ED-citation gate on day one; audit-script consolidation census
description: FOUND BY an independent read-only Fable-5 retention assessment. RANKED #1 DANGER, and it is real. tools/validate_ed_citations.py -- a BLOCKING CI gate -- builds its universe of valid ED ids from registers/ PLUS three directories under deprecated/ (ARCHIVE_GLOBS, :145): deprecated/archives/editorial/, deprecated/archives/editorials/, deprecated/canon/. That is 26 files spanning roughly ED-001..ED-1200. R-DEPRECATED evacuated all of them while R-INFRA kept the gate. The gate's OWN docstring (:347-350) records the cost of losing just ONE of those dirs: universe 1167 -> 1107, and 110 VALID citations became NONEXISTENT. NONEXISTENT is never deferred (:377-381). So the evacuation commit would have turned a blocking gate red, and the tempting field fix -- suppress NONEXISTENT -- would have destroyed the repo's only anti-fabrication citation check. The semantic at risk is ED-IN-0075's: an ARCHIVED ed is LEGITIMATE, not missing. A partial ED universe cannot distinguish a typo from a fabrication from a correctly-archived id, so it is strictly worse than either keeping everything or retiring the gate outright. FIX: the 26 files RELOCATE to registers/archive/ instead of evacuating -- which is also exactly Jordan's 'start fresh for registers': a frozen archive beside the active register, new work on a clean surface, provenance intact. Execution note carried in the rule: add 'registers/archive/' to ARCHIVE_GLOBS in the same commit and re-run the gate to confirm the universe size is unchanged. Pinned by test_the_ed_universe_survives_evacuation. AUDIT-SCRIPT CONSOLIDATION (Jordan: 'gather and consolidate all those random audit python scripts that get called'). Censused all 85 .py under audit/ + research/. A first pass on basename substring reported 22 as called by kept executables; reading them showed MOST are PROVENANCE CITATIONS IN COMMENTS, not calls -- e.g. sigma_leverage.py:104 '[canonical: audit/2026-06-03-contest-groundup/engine.py]' and weapon_physics.py:75 cite paths they never import. Same over-report shape as the substring reader scan (ED-IN-0130); corrected by looking for real load idioms (spec_from_file_location / _load_by_path / sys.path.insert / subprocess). TRUE RESULT: the kept tree has essentially ONE executable dependency on audit/ -- tools/gen_sigma_parity_goldens.py:95 loading the contest-groundup parity oracle. The only other references, audit/scripts/vector_audit.py and audit/scripts/structure_audit.py in 3 .claude workflows and 2 .github workflows, are a PHANTOM PATH: audit/scripts/ does not exist (verified), and both scripts actually live in skills/valoria-vector-audit/scripts/. That is one of the 9 undeclared indirections ci_claude_workflow_paths.py already reports; filed, not fixed here, since it touches .claude/ and .github/. CONSOLIDATION EXECUTED IN THE PLAN: the parity oracle relocates to engine/reference/contest-groundup/ -- the PRE-DESIGNED home, since build_fork.py:70 already maps the other parity oracle (tests/sim/v32-combat-balance) to engine/reference/. Its docstring claimed it 'cannot move' because sibling files do `from engine import ...`; that constraint DISSOLVES under evacuation, because those siblings are one-off session code that leaves. Both frozen reference implementations end up in one place beside the code they validate, and audit/ ends with zero executable dependents. GODOT RE-IMPLEMENTS (Jordan, 2026-08-04), so the Python-as-oracle role is CONFIRMED load-bearing and the oracle question is settled: two implementations of the same rules means parity testing is mandatory, not optional. Recorded because the alternative (Godot consuming the typed layer rather than re-implementing) would have dissolved the whole parity burden, and it was considered. title: Standing gate: an adversarial steelmanned read-only review after EVERY milestone, not at the end
description: RULED (Jordan, 2026-08-04): 'use Fable 5 after every milestone/step to do an adversarial steelman read-only review for accuracy and logic and fidelity to plan'. Recorded in systems/_architecture/repository_keep_set_v1.md section 7.1 as a gate on every step of the evacuation sequence: a step is not complete until the review has run and its findings are applied or explicitly refused with a reason. WHAT THIS ADDS TO EXISTING DOCTRINE. CLAUDE.md section 10 already requires the agonist->antagonist relay and already wires valoria-critic (Read/Grep/Glob only, so independence is structural rather than declared, ED-IN-0087). It does NOT specify a CADENCE. This does: per MILESTONE, not per programme. JUSTIFIED FROM THIS PROGRAMME'S OWN RECORD, not from principle. Three defects in the separation work were found by adversarial passes and by nothing else, each invisible to the instrument that had just been built and pronounced sound: (1) the contest-groundup parity oracle sat in the evacuate set while a kept tool loads it to regenerate a committed golden a kept CI test asserts on (ED-IN-0130); (2) readers() could not see split paths, so the blocking-reader counts that sequence the entire deletion were blind to os.path.join construction -- 45 readers missed (ED-IN-0130); (3) deprecated/ holds 26 files of the BLOCKING ED-citation gate's universe, so the evacuation commit would have turned that gate red and the tempting fix would have destroyed the repo's only anti-fabrication check (ED-IN-0131). Each was cheap to check and expensive to have acted on. A single end-of-programme review would have caught all three AFTER the work they invalidate. THREE PROPERTIES THE GATE MUST KEEP or it decays into ceremony: (a) read-only BY CONSTRUCTION -- route through valoria-critic, never a prompt that merely declares read-only, since a sentence inside a prompt restricts nothing; (b) STEELMAN FIRST -- the reviewer states the strongest case for the work before attacking it, and 'this is correct and here is the best argument for it' is a valid verdict; (c) THE REVIEWER'S CLAIMS ARE CHECKED TOO -- reviews have been wrong in this programme (one reported id_reservations next_free unbumped when it was bumped; it had read a mid-session snapshot), so an audit is evidence, not a verdict. NOT YET ENFORCED. This is a convention with no guard. A CI check cannot observe whether a review ran, so the honest options are a per-step artifact under audit/ or a required line in the step's commit message. Filed rather than asserted -- per CLAUDE.md 0.1 point 5, if the guard cannot be written the pattern is not yet understood, and I am not claiming enforcement I have not built.

title: CORRECTION ROW: ED-IN-0131's 'phantom audit/scripts/ path' claim is WRONG and is retracted
description: CORRECTION ROW (append-only; retracts one claim in ED-IN-0131, registers/editorial_ledger_in.jsonl:58). THE RETRACTED CLAIM: 'audit/scripts/vector_audit.py and audit/scripts/structure_audit.py in 3 .claude workflows and 2 .github workflows are a PHANTOM PATH: audit/scripts/ does not exist (verified), and both scripts actually live in skills/valoria-vector-audit/scripts/. That is one of the 9 undeclared indirections ci_claude_workflow_paths.py already reports.' IT IS FALSE. The workflows never named audit/scripts/ at all. They name the full, correct, existing path skills/valoria-vector-audit/scripts/vector_audit.py -- e.g. .github/workflows/dashboard.yml:87, .github/workflows/audit-refresh.yml:83. My extraction grep was `audit/[a-z0-9./_-]+\.py`, which matched the SUBSTRING 'audit/scripts/vector_audit.py' inside 'valoria-vector-AUDIT/SCRIPTS/vector_audit.py'. A controlled re-grep for the literal not preceded by a word character or hyphen -- `(^|[^-a-zA-Z0-9_/])audit/scripts/` -- finds EXACTLY ONE occurrence in the entire tree: inside ED-IN-0131's own description. The only place the phantom path exists is the entry claiming it exists. WHY THIS IS WORTH A ROW RATHER THAN A QUIET EDIT. It is the THIRD instance of one defect class in this programme -- an unanchored substring match producing a false positive -- and ED-IN-0131 CORRECTS THAT EXACT CLASS TWICE IN ITS OWN TEXT (the 22-callers over-report, and ED-IN-0130's split-path scan). I diagnosed the disease in the same paragraph in which I contracted it. The lesson is not 'be careful with grep'; it is that a path-shaped regex needs a LEFT ANCHOR (start-of-line or a non-path character) or it silently matches mid-token, and no amount of care substitutes for the anchor. ALSO CORRECTED, from the same review: (a) keys.py:183's docstring says a '44-type roster'; the registry actually has 55 `### family.type` headings and tools/build_key_graph.py:7 says 55 -- a stale hand-maintained count in the loader for the very file it parses. Any inversion must repoint all five. (c) tools/handoff_atomize.py is blocked on TWO Jordan calls, not one (HANDOFF_IN.md:542). (d) systems/_architecture/repository_keep_set_v1.md:144,:151 still state the superseded 2026-07-21 cutoff and :157 still lists workplans/ and dashboard/ as evacuating. NO ACTION was taken on the false claim beyond this retraction: nothing was fixed on its basis, because it was explicitly 'filed, not fixed here'. The harm was bounded to the record, which is precisely why the record gets corrected. title: W4a: the Key-type registry is cooked to typed JSON; runtime reads data, markdown stays authored
description: W4a of the separation work list (HANDOFF_IN). The clearest data-in-prose violation in the tree, named as 'the clearest inversion' by the fork plan §4.1 and unexecuted until now. WHAT WAS WRONG. systems/_architecture/key_type_registry_v30.md is a REGISTRY PARSED AT RUNTIME. keys.py said so in its own docstring: 'the registry markdown is the single source of truth... this class parses it at load time'. That was correct when the alternative was a hand-copied roster. It stopped being correct for two measured reasons. (a) GODOT RE-IMPLEMENTS THE LOGIC (Jordan, 2026-08-04) and cannot parse markdown; the port's answer today is godot/skeleton/data/key_types/*.tres -- FOUR HAND-MADE files covering 4 of 55 types, 93% incomplete before it starts drifting. (b) THE ROSTER HAS FOUR INDEPENDENT PARSERS, measured this session: engine/substrate/keys.py (TypeRegistry), tools/build_key_graph.py:136, tools/observability/build_graph.py:82 (parse_key_registry), and tools/dashboard_data.py:763 (a `### ` line counter) -- plus a hand-typed family table in dashboard_data.build_keys(). 'Every rule lives once' violated four ways on the most load-bearing registry in the repo, and every hand-maintained count had already drifted (keys.py's own docstring said 44 for a 55-type file, ED-IN-0134). WHAT LANDED. tools/export_key_types.py cooks the markdown to engine/engine_params/key_types.json, following the established typed-export convention (_generated header, schema_version, source, --check round-trip). It does NOT re-parse: it CALLS TypeRegistry.load, because that tolerant line-based parser IS the schema definition (the registry's ```yaml blocks are prose-flavoured -- unquoted colons and parentheticals make strict yaml.safe_load fail on real canonical entries), and a second parser here would re-commit the duplication the tool exists to end. TypeRegistry.load now DISPATCHES ON SUFFIX, so a caller switches source by changing a path constant and nothing else. ORD-1 PRESERVED, and this was nearly got wrong: keys.py:190 records that dict order IS registry order and significant. json.dumps(sort_keys=True) would have been byte-stabler and would have silently destroyed an ordering invariant. The export does not sort; byte-stability comes from the source order being deterministic. Pinned by asserting list(json.types) == list(md.types), not just dict equality. BEHAVIOUR PRESERVED, MEASURED NOT ASSERTED. The runtime reader (engine/cross_scale/echo_transport.py) now loads the JSON, and a seeded campaign returns hash c2da472354077b9c -- byte-identical to the value the fork build produced at the start of this session, before any of this work. FALSIFIERS (three, all green; 32 tests in the file). test_json_and_markdown_registries_are_identical -- the cooked and authored surfaces must parse to the same registry in the same order; this is the entire safety of keeping two surfaces. test_export_round_trips_byte_exact -- --check passes against the committed file. test_the_round_trip_check_can_fail -- POSITIVE CONTROL: plants a mutation in the committed JSON, asserts the checker exits 1 with DRIFT, restores, and then re-checks that the restore itself was clean so the test cannot poison the tree. Without it, --check passing would prove only that it ran. Also: the earlier roster pin was tightened from `>= 44` to exact three-way equality in ED-IN-0135 SPECIFICALLY so this inversion could not silently drop types -- that guard was put in place one commit before the work it guards, which is the point of the ED-IN-0132 cadence. WIRED: valoria-ci.yml validators job, tools/valoria_local.py (blocking), and references/ci_checks_registry.yaml. DELIBERATELY NOT DONE -- W4b. The three TOOL-side parsers (build_key_graph, build_graph, dashboard_data) still read the markdown with their own parsers. Repointing four parsers in one commit is where mistakes happen, and the runtime was the priority. The inversion is therefore PARTIAL and this entry says so rather than claiming completion: markdown is still machine-read by three tools. W4b consolidates them onto TypeRegistry.load(JSON) and deletes dashboard_data's hand-typed family table. Also deferred: regenerating the 4 .tres from the JSON (W4c) -- the duplication is now MECHANICALLY REMOVABLE, which it was not before today. MEASURED-BY: tools/export_key_types.py --check -- 55 types, round-trip OK. MEASURED-BY: tests/valoria/test_key_substrate.py -- 32 tests; the mutation control forces exit 1. MEASURED-BY: seeded campaign via engine.mc_v18 -- key_log_hash c2da472354077b9c, unchanged.

title: W4a regression: a new CI command was added without declaring it — caught by the full suite, not by targeted tests
description: REGRESSION FROM W4a (ED-IN-0136), found by the full tests/valoria suite and by nothing else. W4a wired `python3 tools/export_key_types.py --check` into .github/workflows/valoria-ci.yml. tests/valoria/test_gate_coverage.py::test_no_phantom_command_was_introduced diffs the set of commands the workflow actually invokes against a declared EXPECTED_COMMANDS list, and correctly flagged the addition as undeclared. Fixed by registering the command (its own failure message says the remedy: 'A new validator is fine -- add it here'). 13 tests in the file green. THE LESSON, which is CLAUDE.md 0.1's 'targeted-green is not validation' landing on me directly. Before committing W4a I ran: the targeted key-substrate tests (32 green), the evacuation-plan tests, and `valoria_local.py --staged` (all local gates passed). None of them run pytest's gate-coverage test, so all three were green while a real regression sat in the changeset. The tests I wrote for the thing I built encoded my model of it, not the system -- exactly the failure 0.1 describes. The guard that caught it exists because of an earlier incident of the same family: its docstring records that a report-only step written as `echo \"::group::python3 tools/X.py\"; python3 tools/X.py` made the parser capture the closing quote into the args, yielding 10 phantom commands that `--ci` would have tried to execute -- 'caught by diffing the command set before/after rather than by reading the YAML'. A declared-set diff catches both additions and malformations; reading the YAML catches neither. ALSO IN THIS ENTRY, two measurement notes recorded because both could have produced a false conclusion. (1) The background full-suite run that surfaced this reported 10 failures against a baseline of 8, but it STARTED BEFORE the last edits and ran against a mid-edit tree -- a confounded measurement in the ED-MB-0042 sense. Decomposed rather than trusted: 8 known MB, 1 stale-bytecode artifact, 1 real. Only the real one was acted on. (2) The stale-bytecode artifact is worth its own note: a mutation run changed AUDIT_CUTOFF '2026-07-01' -> '2026-07-21' (IDENTICAL byte length) and restored via `cp` within the same mtime second; Python's staleness check is (mtime, size), so it served the mutant .pyc and a test read a value that was not on disk. Clearing tools/__pycache__ restored green. The mutation-testing pattern this session relies on can silently poison later runs whenever the mutation preserves file size -- and a staleness check that cannot see a change is the same defect class this programme keeps correcting. title: W4a gate response: load_json was a WEAKER validator than the markdown path, and I re-committed the stale-quotation defect inside the docstring that lectures about it
description: Response to the ED-IN-0132 gate review of W4a (verdict COMPLETE-WITH-RESIDUALS). The review's steelman held on the core -- one parser, ORD-1 defended at every layer it could reach, the mutation control competent, the guard landed one commit before the work it guards. Two real defects and one fidelity finding. R1 -- THE VALIDATOR ASYMMETRY, and it is the one that mattered. load_json checked only 'types is a non-empty dict'. The MARKDOWN path gets two guarantees structurally for free: the heading regex [a-z_]+.[a-z_]+ makes a malformed type id UNREPRESENTABLE, and _parse_entry always returns a dict. So the JSON path was strictly weaker than the path it is replacing. PROVEN, not argued: {'types': {'NotAnId': 42}} LOADED. Tolerable while echo_transport is the only consumer of a CI-pinned file; not tolerable when W4b binds three more consumers and W4c binds Godot -- a weaker validator on the path that is BECOMING PRIMARY is the wrong direction. Fixed to parity: type-id shape (sharing a compiled pattern with the heading regex so the two loaders cannot disagree about what a valid id is), entry-is-dict, and a type_count cross-check that uses the count the document already carries instead of letting it rot unread. Falsifiers: three parametrized rejection tests plus a positive control that the tightened validator still accepts the real 55-type registry. 36 tests in the file. R2 -- I RE-COMMITTED THE STALE-QUOTATION DEFECT, in the docstring that documents it. tools/export_key_types.py quoted keys.py's OLD docstring in the present tense -- and the same commit rewrote that docstring, so the quotation was FALSE ON ARRIVAL. It also cited keys.py:208-239 for the tolerant parser (now :241) and keys.py:190 for the ORD-1 comment (now :203); both shifted because the same commit inserted load_json above them. This is the THIRD instance in this programme (ED-IN-0133 the unanchored grep, ED-IN-0135 the unswept 44-type quote), and the second where the defect appears inside prose warning about the defect. The fix is not 'be careful': it is that prose about code must DESCRIBE or cite something that does not shift. Line numbers in a file that is being edited are a self-inflicted staleness generator, and quoting a file you are changing in the same commit is guaranteed to be wrong. Rewritten to describe rather than quote, with the reasoning left in place so the next session inherits the rule and not just the correction. SWEPT, not spot-fixed. Also stale and now corrected: keys.py's MODULE docstring still said the roster was 'parsed at load time -- the registry markdown remains the single source of truth; nothing is duplicated here', contradicting its own class docstring 165 lines below; and tools/dashboard_data.py:794 still described TypeRegistry as parsing the markdown at runtime. A repo-wide re-grep for 'parses the markdown|parsed at load time|parses it at load' now returns nothing -- the sweep is the point, since the survivor in dashboard_data was one I would not have remembered to check. R3 -- FIDELITY FINDING, FLAGGED NOT SILENTLY RESOLVED. Fork plan §4.1 specifies the JSON becomes SOURCE with 'the markdown table regenerated as documentation', and its §4 table files key_types.json under SOURCE (data). W4a shipped the REVERSE polarity: markdown stays authored/source, JSON is GENERATED. That is defensible -- it keeps one human-reviewable authored surface and matches the export_engine_params precedent -- but it means the fragile prose-flavoured tolerant parser stays load-bearing FOREVER, which retiring was §4.1's actual point. ED-IN-0136 cited §4.1 as its mandate without noting the reversal. Per CLAUDE.md §2 divergence must be LOUD, so it is recorded here and carried to Jordan rather than settled by me: making JSON the source is a one-way door on where a human edits a key type. ALSO FILED from the review, not acted on: the four hand-made .tres have ALREADY drifted -- scene_combat_strike.tres has optional_payload_fields ['commit'] where the registry has ['commit','weapon']. So W4c's 'regenerate and byte-compare' will go RED, correctly, and that red is a real Godot-side behaviour change rather than a generator bug. Stating it now so a future session does not debug the generator. MEASURED-BY: tests/valoria/test_key_substrate.py -- 36 passed; three malformed registries rejected that previously loaded. title: engine/params/ flips KEEP -> EVACUATE: the 43 parameter-table .md captured byte-lossless into YAML first; and the slice report's first sub-root evacuation exposed two false-positive scans
description: Jordan, 2026-08-04: 'params .md are largely useless at this point and I want them gone. code should have superseded them all by now' / 'just dump the constants to a yaml' / 'provenance can cite to a fork'. evacuation_plan.py's R-PARAMS-INFO rule said KEEP ('prose WITH a code pair -> information only'), justified by ~50 provenance referents from kept code that a deletion would orphan; the fork-citation ruling dissolves that objection, so the rule is now R-PARAMS-DUMPED (evacuate). WHAT WAS NOT ASSUMED. The census that motivated this -- 295 of 378 ALL-CAPS identifiers found in code (78%) -- is an OPTIMISTIC UPPER BOUND and its residue was noise (capitalised prose ALIGNMENT/DISTILLED, HTML markers AUD1, character names ALDRIC/MARET); a name appearing in code never proved its VALUE matched. So the deletion is NOT gated on that measurement. tools/export_params_constants.py captures the tables structurally (file -> section -> header + rows, cells verbatim, no invented schema -- typing them would be authorship) AND stores every file's full text in a `raw` map, making the capture lossless BY CONSTRUCTION rather than by my parser being total. It is not: six files (index stubs, history/) yield no table at all, which is exactly how a silent loss would have happened. Measured: 43/43 files captured, every one byte-identical to source, 258 tables, 1367 rows. THE GATE IS DELIBERATELY TEMPORARY. `--check` re-derives from engine/params/, so it cannot survive its own source; it is wired blocking in all four places (valoria-ci.yml, valoria_local.py, ci_checks_registry.yaml, test_gate_coverage.EXPECTED_COMMANDS -- the exact four-way omission that caused the ED-IN-0137 regression) and must be retired in the SAME commit that deletes engine/params/. No vacuous-pass-on-absent-source path exists, so forgetting turns CI loudly red rather than quietly green. TWO SCAN DEFECTS THE FLIP EXPOSED, both false-positive classes that would have made the deletion report unreadable. (1) engine/ is the FIRST root that only partly evacuates; readers() scanned kept files for the top-level directory, so a 43-file slice reported 'engine/' hits across nearly the whole tree. Fixed with slice_prefixes(): a slice is the shortest prefix under which NOTHING is retained. This also retroactively tightens tests/ and deprecated/, which had the same looseness. (2) joined_path_readers() counted a constructed path as a breakage if ANYTHING under it evacuated; tests/sim holds both evacuating stress prose and the KEPT canon mass-battle engine, so all 30 kept readers of the canon engine were reported as silent breakages. Now requires the target to be WHOLLY evacuating. Split-path alarms fell 33 -> 4, and the four remaining are real. RESULT (re-measured post-commit, when the 3 new files are tracked): 3153 tracked -> 1653 keep + 33 relocate = 1686 retained / 1467 evacuate. The pre-flip figure was 1693 keep + 33 relocate = 1726 retained, so the flip moves 43 files and the 3 new tool/test/data files return 3. CORRECTION (gate review F5): the first version of this entry wrote '1683 keep (was 1650)', comparing keep+relocate against keep-only -- an apples-to-oranges aside, and the kind of unreconciled number this ledger exists to stop. The headline share is unaffected: markdown share of the retained tree 51.9% -> 50.6%. The params tree was a small dent; audit/ (493 kept .md across 59 units, under Jordan's July rule) is 58% of all retained markdown and is the only remaining lever worth more than a percentage point. GATE REVIEW RESPONSE (ED-IN-0132 pass, verdict COMPLETE-WITH-RESIDUALS; fixes landed in the follow-up commit). F1 THE HEADLINE CLAIM WAS UNGUARDED: the exporter read text-mode with errors='ignore' and the falsifier verified with the IDENTICAL lossy read, so a CRLF line or an undecodable byte would be normalised/dropped on both sides and the pair would agree with each other while diverging from the file -- two lossy reads that match are not evidence of losslessness. Now reads bytes and decodes strictly (an invalid byte raises rather than vanishing) and the test compares raw bytes against the capture re-encoded. Measured: zero CR bytes across the 43 files, so the dump is byte-unchanged; what changed is what happens to a file that arrives before the deletion slice. F2 SCOPE GAP: the rule evacuates engine/params/** while the capture globbed **/*.md AND the test used the same filter -- guard and capture shared a blind spot (glob also skips dotfiles). Both now walk the tree; the exporter refuses to write if any file is outside the capture glob. Empty today, which is luck, not design. F3 THE CONTROL COVERED ONLY THE COMPLETENESS BRANCH -- it planted an omission, not a mismatch, so the byte comparison carrying the word 'byte-identical' had no falsifier at all, and this entry described the control as stronger than it was. Four content mutations added (cell delimiter, trailing newline, LF->CRLF, one digit). F4 a stale '1,996 files' survived in test_evacuation_plan.py's docstring in the same commit that changed the count to 1467 -- the ED-IN-0134/0138 stale-quotation class again, now removed rather than restated. F6 CLAUDE.md 5 still taught engine/params/ as the live number surface and listed the typed round-trip-checked export as 'not yet built'; amended. F7 the local references/evacuation_manifest.json was stale but is gitignored and untracked -- regenerated. F8 the reviewer swept for true positives lost to the scan tightening and found none. NOT ACCEPTED AS DEFECTS: nothing; all six actionable findings were taken.
