title: W1: the nine known-red mass-battle tests carried as strict xfail from one register, so the shipping gate stops requiring a manual differential to read
description: ED-MB-0061 records the cost exactly: the merge that turned main red left the failure set unrecorded, so 'no other lane could distinguish a new regression from the known set'. This branch paid that cost three times -- each CI failure needed a re-run of the suite against origin/main in a detached worktree and a hand diff of the lists to establish that none of the nine were mine. A gate that requires a manual differential is not a gate; the risk is not the nine failures but the tenth nobody notices. A REGISTER, NOT NINE DECORATORS: tests/valoria/conftest.py owns the set and applies it at collection, so the excused set is countable and reviewable in one place (CLAUDE.md section 8's every-rule-lives-once). strict=True is deliberate -- a non-strict xfail absorbs a FIX as well as a failure, so the MB lane would get no signal when its work lands; strict means a test that starts passing turns the suite red and forces the register updated in the same commit. The register therefore cannot rot in the passing direction, and test_known_red_register.py stops it rotting in the other: every id must name a file and a def that exist (a stale entry excuses a test that is gone and hides one that is not), the count is pinned at 9 so growth by accretion requires a deliberate commit, and every entry must cite ED-MB-0061 so the mechanism cannot start absorbing unrelated failures. SCOPE: no mass-battle code, config, golden or threshold is touched. Jordan clarified 2026-08-04 that 'stop worrying about MB' meant stop trying to solve MB gameplay/coding issues, not stop repo work that touches MB test files -- and the ED-IN-0132 audit of the programme independently found W1 recorded in this repo's own work list as 'precondition: none / independent, parallelisable now', with no MB-scope block anywhere in the tree. The block existed only in chat and contradicted the register it was blocking. It cost the branch its whole length.

title: The audit ruling's SECOND clause finally implemented ('none for infrastructure'), plus the working-paper join: 493 kept audit .md -> 119, and the first 164 files actually deleted
description: THE DEFECT, found by the ED-IN-0132 adversarial audit of the programme and not by me: Jordan ruled TWO things -- 'probably keep audits from july overall' AND 'Audit history for all of July, but none for infrastructure'. Only the first reached the tree. The string 'none for infrastructure' appeared NOWHERE in the repository, and R-AUDIT-RECENT had become the single largest keep rule in the partition (675 files, ~40% of the entire retained tree) on half a ruling. This is precisely the failure the separation work list's own preamble was written to close -- 'the plan was not in the tree; a gate that cannot be checked is ceremony' -- recurring one level up, on a ruling rather than a plan. CLASSIFIER: the unit's DOMINANT cited ED-<LANE> tag, not my reading of 59 directory names. The repo already has a lane vocabulary and each audit unit's own citations say where its findings belong. Jordan ruled this form directly: 'we would only keep design lane dominant stuff'. KNOWN OVER-CAPTURE, disclosed before the ruling and ruled on with eyes open: a lane tag records who FILED an item, not what it is ABOUT, and cross-cutting design work gets IN ids by convention. Jordan then ruled the single largest casualty back in by name -- 'emergent narrative to be kept but joined appropriately' -- so AUDIT_KEEP_OVERRIDE holds it as an explicit named exception with the quote attached. Units citing no ED at all (the contest-gate packets, scene-combat redesign) have no dominant lane and are NOT infrastructure by default; they are KEPT, because evacuating them would be inferring a ruling that was not given. THE JOIN (Jordan: 'we can keep the nested working papers so long as they are filed very cleanly or we can join them all together and purge the excess'). tools/join_audit_workings.py concatenates a unit's nested tier into one _workings_joined.md, each fragment between delimiters carrying its original path, bytes copied verbatim -- nothing summarised, reflowed or renumbered, so nothing interpreted can be misinterpreted. It VERIFIES BEFORE IT PURGES: re-splits the joined document and compares every fragment against source bytes, and refuses to delete anything that does not round-trip byte-exactly. The tests were written BEFORE it ran, because after a purge the property is unfalsifiable against sources that no longer exist -- with controls for the three ways concatenate-and-split silently loses content: a body containing delimiter-shaped text, trailing-newline eating, and empty files. Six surviving units joined, 164 fragments -> 6 files, all verified. RESULT: tracked 3144 (branch point) -> 2999, the FIRST files this programme has actually removed after 17 commits of instrument-building that deleted nothing. Kept audit .md 493 -> 119. Retained tree if every slice lands 1686 -> 1275, markdown share 50.6% -> 37.6%, and .py (511) now outnumbers .md (479) for the first time.

title: Two gate defects the identifier census exposed: a blocking citation gate double-counting quotations, and a drift gate that could not fail
description: BOTH FOUND BY CI ON THE SAME PUSH, both in the class 'a gate that reports the wrong thing stops being read'. (1) GENERATED INVENTORIES QUOTE CITATIONS; THEY DO NOT MAKE THEM. systems/<sub>/_identifier_census.yaml records the table row or sentence each identifier appears in, quoted VERBATIM because summarising would be authorship -- so it carries the design docs' own ED references. validate_ed_citations scans systems/, and read the inventory as ASSERTING an open ED as its basis: 17 OPEN_AS_BASIS violations, every one a double-count of a citation already counted in the source doc, turning a BLOCKING gate red on noise. Exempted, with a deliberately NARROW two-condition predicate so it cannot become an escape hatch: basename starts with '_' AND the file carries the literal 'GENERATED by tools/' banner. A hand-authored doc cannot buy the exemption by being renamed; a generated file cannot buy it by dropping its banner. VERIFIED NOT TO WEAKEN THE GATE, because _walk() builds BOTH the scan set and the ED UNIVERSE and this tool's own docstring records a universe shrink (1167->1107) turning 110 valid citations into NONEXISTENT: measured after the change, universe 1193 unchanged, archive files 26 unchanged, deferred 10 unchanged, violations 17 -> 0. (2) A DRIFT GATE THAT CANNOT FAIL IS DECORATION. build_test_register.py --check printed fresh statistics and exited 0 UNCONDITIONALLY -- it never compared against the committed register. So references/test_register.json went stale THREE TIMES in one session (after the audit-workings purge, after W1's new test modules, after test_pathres.py) and every time it was tests/valoria/test_test_register.py in CI that noticed, never the tool that owns the artifact and never the local hook. Local-green while CI-red is exactly how a local tier stops being trusted. --check now diffs and exits 1; wired blocking into valoria_local.py AND valoria-ci.yml AND declared in test_gate_coverage.EXPECTED_COMMANDS (the four-way wiring whose omission caused ED-IN-0137). It failed on its first run, on the stale register I had just created -- which is the only evidence that a new gate works.

title: Audit-family critique: which are load-bearing, and what the staleness metric actually measures
description: Filed as P8 during the W4 gate ("needs Jordan's call on which audit families are load-bearing"); this is the evidence for that call. Document: audit/2026-07-30-audit-family-critique/00_critique.md. HEADLINE. The vector audit IS the thing that identifies what is missing and nothing else in the repo computes it, AND its findings are near-stationary. Both are true at once and the staleness metric conflates them. MEASURED: over 8 days and 240 files of in-scope churn the feed moved 3 rows out of 178, in the improving direction (isolates 9->7, sparse_context 16->15; implied_missing 35 and notional 100 byte-stable). A freshness warning on a stationary backlog measures the wrong axis -- it says 're-run a script' when the message should be '178 structural gaps have gone unworked'. RECOMMENDATION 1 is therefore to INVERT what it reports (backlog counts, not drift), NOT to demote it; an earlier draft of this analysis recommended demotion and that was wrong, for the reason the two-axis split in the document's section 1 gives (content value and staleness informativeness are uncorrelated here). PER-FAMILY: mechanics-index is the one to promote -- it has NO generator, so its drift is editorial debt no script can clear, and it is the smallest number on the banner. vector-audit is highest on content value, lowest on staleness informativeness (both production paths regenerate the feed immediately before consuming it). graph-lexicon is low on both. decisions/proposals/apparatus are the governance observatory, NOT part of the vectorization review at all -- only vector-audit (its output), graph-lexicon (soft input) and mechanics-index (cited input) touch skills/valoria-vector-audit/. npc-audit should be reclassified: its artifact is an AUTHORED document, so 'stale' means a human must re-audit, sharing no remedy with 're-run a script'. THREE METRIC DEFECTS. D1: drift is computed from the artifact's last git COMMIT, not its last regeneration, so a no-op regen commits nothing and drift accumulates forever while the artifact is provably current -- not firing today (regeneration does change content) but silent when it does. D2: the weekly cron is nominally weekly, actually 1-in-3 -- exactly ONE scheduled refresh has ever landed (4029870, PR #244, 2026-07-27), the only commit matching the bot's own message; vector-audit and graph-lexicon last moved 07-22 and were not updated by the 07-27 run. D3: scope over-breadth manufactures the headline -- vector-audit's scope is most of the repo, so 240 files of churn produced 3 changed rows; the code carries a prior correction for exactly this failure mode at a smaller scope. THREE OF THIS ANALYSIS'S OWN HYPOTHESES WERE WRONG and were corrected by reading rather than grepping: ci_naming_check does NOT consume lexicon.json (it EXCLUDES it, skip-list at :70); review_core does NOT read apparatus_registry.yaml (comment only, :52); and the graph.json-pinned CI drift guard described at vector_audit.py:1215-1222 NO LONGER EXISTS -- the guard was rewritten to remove the dependency, so that docstring is STALE (recorded, not fixed: it is a skills/ file and this was a read-only critique). LIMITS STATED, NOT HIDDEN: notional (100) is untriaged, so the honest reading is 42 sharp findings (35 implied-missing + 7 isolates) + 136 needing triage, NOT 178 actionable; the stationarity claim is one regeneration at one commit; consumer analysis is static grep-then-read and would miss a dynamic import. Seven recommendations, ALL HELD -- none executed. PROVENANCE: the backlog counts and the 178->175 stationarity delta are reproduced by MEASURED-BY: skills/valoria-vector-audit/scripts/vector_audit.py (run with --emit-findings and diff against the committed feed); the per-family drift figures and scope definitions by MEASURED-BY: tools/audit_staleness.py; the regeneration-changes-content test for D1 by MEASURED-BY: tools/observability/build_decisions.py (run, then git diff --stat its artifact). Section 7 of the document carries the exact commands.
source: audit/2026-07-30-audit-family-critique/00_critique.md; tools/audit_staleness.py; .github/workflows/audit-refresh.yml
falsifier: Section 7 of the document is a runnable reproduction block. The stationarity claim falsifies by re-emitting the feed and finding a large delta; D2 falsifies by `git log --all --grep='Scheduled decisions-digest'` returning more than one commit; the three corrected hypotheses falsify by reading ci_naming_check.py:70, review_core.py:52 and tests/valoria/test_vector_audit.py's rederivation guard.

title: The keep-set for the code-first main, authored fresh — CARRY/LEAVE cannot be run backwards without deleting the enforcement tier
description: ARTIFACT: systems/_architecture/repository_keep_set_v1.md. It is the partition of record for the evacuate direction ruled in ED-IN-0125, and it SUPERSEDES tools/build_fork.py's CARRY/LEAVE for that purpose. needs_jordan TRUE for its per-directory table only: the four rules it applies are Jordan's words from the 2026-08-04 session and are RATIFIED; the application of those rules to 16 directories is this document's inference and is vetoable row by row. No deletion is authorised by it. WHY AUTHORED FRESH RATHER THAN INVERTED. audit/2026-08-03-session-oddities.md section M recommends 'git rm everything that is not in CARRY'. That assumes CARRY union LEAVE partitions the tree. IT DOES NOT. The neither-set includes .github/, .githooks/, .claude/, tools/, tests/valoria/, most of references/, research/, skills/, and the root files CLAUDE.md / CURRENT.md / HANDOFF.md. Under EXTRACT the neither-set defaults to left-behind (harmless); under EVACUATE the same command DELETES it -- the entire CLAUDE.md section 8 enforcement tier, the shipping gate, and the session protocol. LEAVE further conflates prose contamination with SOURCE-REPO INFRASTRUCTURE, whose two rationales are extraction-only by their own wording: tools/ 'the fork re-derives what it needs' and tests/valoria/ 'engine/tests comes instead'. Under keep-main tests/valoria/ is the shipping gate AND the home of the fork plan's own falsifiers (test_faction_l_reconstruction, test_key_graph, test_execution_map, test_public_governance_transfer_key, test_morale_write_sweep) -- evacuating it would delete the guards every step of the plan cites. That command must not be run. THE SECOND FILTER, because age alone fails: audit/2026-07-29-scenario-visualization/ is 36 MB (21 PNGs + an 11 MB HTML) and SIX DAYS OLD, so a pure two-week rule keeps it. Generated artifacts evacuate; their generators stay -- Jordan wants mass-battle and eventually grid-based scene-combat map visualizations, so the four .py generators there are assets and arguably belong in tools/. THE CUT IS PER-FILE, NOT PER-ROOT, and two measured cases prove it: engine/params/ is 584K of prose INSIDE the engine keep-root, and tests/sim/mass_battle/ is the canon MB engine (28 .py, ZERO .md) inside an otherwise-evacuating parent. 'JUDICIOUS' MEASURED: 99 of 102 tools are referenced by CI, hooks, .claude/ or another tool -- the dead-tool prune already happened, so orphan-hunting yields about one tool. The real criterion is SUBJECT: a tool retires or re-scopes in the SAME COMMIT as the tree it serves (audit_staleness, scope_ratchet, dashboard_data, ci_register_size_check, ci_audit_registry_check, and the observability suite all read evacuating trees). title: The keep/relocate/evacuate partition as a guarded instrument, not a prose table
description: WHY A TOOL. ED-IN-0127 authored the keep-set as prose. Prose cannot be executed or checked, and the specific failure being guarded against is one that PROSE CANNOT CATCH: build_fork.py's CARRY and LEAVE read like a partition and are not one. CARRY union LEAVE leaves a large NEITHER set (.github/, .githooks/, .claude/, tools/, tests/valoria/, most of references/, research/, skills/, CLAUDE.md, CURRENT.md, HANDOFF.md). Under EXTRACT the neither-set defaults to left-behind, which is harmless; under EVACUATE the mirror operation deletes it, taking the enforcement tier, the shipping gate and the session protocol. The defect was in NEITHER LIST -- it was in the assumption that two lists cover the tree. So tools/evacuation_plan.py refuses to emit a plan unless the partition is TOTAL over every tracked file. MEASURED: 3146 tracked files -> 1149 KEEP / 6 RELOCATE / 1991 EVACUATE. --check green: partition total; contract guard clean (no contracted or stub unit inside the evacuate set -- a unit with a contract but no code YET is the backlog, not dead weight). Per-slice blocking readers, which are what sequences a safe deletion: tests 73, audit 60, deprecated 24, proposals 16, workplans 16, arcs 9. A slice is ready when its blocking readers are zero or retired in the SAME commit. A THIRD VERDICT, RELOCATE (Jordan, 2026-08-04: 'visualization tool for mb should be moved to mb and wiring should be to systems folder'). keep/evacuate cannot express 'this is ours but filed in the wrong place'. Six MB instruments move to systems/mass_battle/workbench/ -- four from audit/2026-07-29-scenario-visualization/ (measure_colocation.py is the STANDING measurement behind ED-MB-0056/0059, not a session record) and two from research/diagrams/mass_battle_formations/. Precedent: systems/combat/combat_engine_v1/workbench/. Their rendered output does NOT travel; it regenerates from the relocated source. A DEFECT IN MY OWN FIRST DRAFT, found by probing rather than by review, and recorded because the shape recurs: R-AUDIT-GENSRC kept ANY .py under audit/ on the rationale 'a generator, not a record'. It was justified by FOUR visualisation generators and fired on 82 files, ~78 being stale April/May one-off session sims (mc_v10.py, pp686_sim.py, stage10_articulation_sim.py). A keep-rule 20x broader than its justification is precisely how a 'streamlined' repo quietly keeps its detritus. Deleted; ordering does the work instead -- generated output evacuates at any date, then the ordinary two-week rule applies to source, so in-window generators are kept because their session is current and stale sims leave with theirs. R-AUDIT-STALE 1040 -> 1087. DASHBOARD KEPT (Jordan, 2026-08-04), reversing ED-IN-0127's evacuate row. CAVEAT NOT YET RULED: the dashboard's INPUTS shrink -- it surfaces proposals/ BY LOCATION and reads workplans/, and workplans/ is still in the evacuate set with 16 blocking readers including tools/workplan_status.py (the SessionStart banner) and tools/dashboard_data.py. Keeping the dashboard while evacuating its data sources leaves a live surface reading missing files. Flagged, not silently resolved. FALSIFIER (CLAUDE.md 0.1 point 3): tests/valoria/test_evacuation_plan.py, 24 tests, MUTATION-VERIFIED 5/5. (M1) unmatched files default to keep instead of UNPARTITIONED -> 1 failed, caught by test_the_totality_guard_can_fail, the positive control that stops totality being vacuously true. (M2) undated audit entries treated as recent -> 2 failed. (M3) contract guard always clean -> 1 failed. (M4) relocation destinations point back into audit/ -> 1 failed. (M5) generated renders no longer beat the two-week keep -> 2 failed. Tool restored byte-exact after the run (cmp clean); control 24 passed. test_ordering_is_load_bearing pins FIRST-MATCH-WINS specifically: tests/sim/mass_battle/ matches both R-MB-CANON (keep) and R-TESTS-PROSE (evacuate), so a reordering would evacuate the canon engine while totality still passed. SCOPE: NO DELETION IS AUTHORISED BY THIS ENTRY. The tool computes and reports; it never removes a file, and says so in its own docstring. needs_jordan is TRUE for the per-directory line (the workplans/dashboard coupling above, skills/ triage, and the proposals/ per-file list).

title: Process review: the continuity record stopped nine commits short of the tree, a positive control that could not fail, and the systematic cause of five retracted numbers
description: Read-only Fable-5 review of the SESSION METHOD (not its artifacts), verdict SOUND-WITH-DEFECTS. F1, the one that compounds: registers/handoffs/HANDOFF_IN.md had ZERO mentions of pathres, the identifier census, the known-red register or ED-IN-0140/0141/0142, and still marked W1 'open' after ED-IN-0140 executed it; six commits carried no ledger entry, so their findings lived only in commit messages, which no tool reads. A fresh session resuming per CLAUDE.md section 1 would have believed W1 open, not known pathres existed, and not known 164 files were deleted. This is the SAME defect class this session spent the day prosecuting in others -- the 'none for infrastructure' ruling that reached no file. Reconciled. F5, a new defect on a surface nobody had cited: test_known_red_register's test_the_staleness_guard_can_fail asserted only that a planted path did not exist and NEVER FED IT THROUGH the detection logic -- cripple the loop and the control still passed. Verbatim the defect ED-IN-0139 F3 recorded the SAME DAY, committed inside the test file written to prevent it. Predicate extracted to _stale_ids() so the control exercises it, and both staleness directions (file gone, test renamed) now have a control plus a cries-wolf check. Also corrected a stale cross-reference in test_pathres.py claiming a caveat lived in HANDOFF_IN.md; it did not. F2, THE SYSTEMATIC CAUSE OF EVERY RETRACTED NUMBER: each was a FIRST-RUN number from a NEW instrument, reported before that instrument had a control (78% census -> noise; 0 -> 58 citations; phantom audit/scripts/; 39 -> 2; 7 -> 2; four-way -> five-way). CLAUDE.md 0.1 point 4 already forbids this; it was being applied downstream, at the review boundary, instead of at the REPORTING boundary. Adopted rule: no first-run count reaches a ledger entry, commit headline or Jordan without (a) a positive control that plants a known instance the scan must find and (b) a hand-verified sample per bucket -- otherwise it is labelled UNVERIFIED SCAN. F3, the catch ratio, which is the health metric and is unflattering: producer's own controls ~5, antagonist reviews ~20, CI 4, and all four CI catches were pure process misses (the full CI-equivalent existed locally and was not run pre-push). The four-way-wiring omission RECURRED (0137 -> 0142) and the stale-quotation class landed five times. Upstream discipline is real but is not absorbing its own lessons within the session. F7, trajectory: 3144 tracked at branch point -> 3018 now, and the tree RE-GREW 2999 -> 3018 after the single deletion commit as instrument output accumulated inside the tree being shrunk. Falsifiable signal recorded in the handoff: within three commits, one must run W3 or land a W7 slice taking git ls-files below 3018 with the four gates green, or the tooling-programme reading is confirmed. W3's precondition (W1) is already satisfied -- only the stale handoff hid that.

title: W3 deletion rehearsal: the shipping gate does not COLLECT after the cut — a third reader blind spot
description: Executed the partition in a throwaway worktree: 1,724 files deleted, 1,279 tracked. Four blocking gates broke, one predicted. HEADLINE: tests/sim/gauge_mb.py evacuates while two KEPT shipping-gate tests do `import gauge_mb` -- a bare module name. readers() greps for the path string (never appears); joined_path_readers() looks for constructed paths (there is no join). Deleting it does not fail a test, it stops pytest COLLECTING AT ALL -- strictly worse than a red test and invisible to every static prediction. module_import_readers() added, TRANSITIVE (one hop was demonstrably wrong: keeping github_ops.py immediately made its two imports load-bearing), with a false positive killed before reporting (`import engine` resolves to the top-level PACKAGE). title: Post-evacuation cleanup: 24 test failures -> 0, by deleting what lost its subject rather than repairing it
description: Jordan: 'Keep it simple, ie don't build tools unnecessarily.' A read-only review triaged the 24 failures left by the evacuation and found ONE genuinely broken kept tool; everything else was a guard outliving the thing it guarded. Disposition was DELETE by default. DELETED, subject gone: tests/valoria/test_params_dump.py (7 failures -- it existed to make the engine/params deletion safe, and that deletion is now merged; a safety guard for a consumed one-way door guards nothing). tools/ci_formula_prose_check.py + its test + 4 wiring points -- BOTH its inputs left main (the census and its entire live-scan surface), so it was a report-only gate printing 'no drift' over nothing, which its own comment records having happened for 14 days once already. 46 dead LANE_PATH_PREFIXES rows in build_decisions -- a lane-map row matching nothing does not fail loudly, it silently leaves the lane unassigned. Two one-liners: build_proposals' ranked_view (linked at an evacuated doc -- a link nobody can follow is worse than no link) and engine/params/ from validate_ed_citations' scan prefixes. FIXED, genuinely broken: tools/build_identifier_census.py imported parse_file from the retired export_params_constants and ImportError'd on invocation. The 'one owner' deferral was correct when written; deferring to an owner whose subject then leaves makes the dependency the defect. Parser inlined, ~20 lines, no second consumer to drift against. TERMINAL-STATE TEST CASUALTIES, the interesting class: four tests asserted against a NON-EMPTY evacuate set, which is now empty -- the state the tool was built to reach. Asserting the scan finds something is asserting the job is unfinished. Rewritten to plant their own inputs, so the property (a mixed prefix is not evacuating; a constructed path into an evacuating tree is found) survives the success of the thing it was watching. Same shape for test_wf_harness_check, whose fixture COPIED a wf_*.js retired with the evacuation: all 20 tests errored at setup. Synthesising a donor from the owner block was tried and rejected on measurement -- the gate enforces per-script rules a minimal synthetic script fails -- so the last real donor was restored from the fork ref as a committed FIXTURE. Data, not tooling. CLAUDE.md section 3 corrected: it still described arcs/ as a live primary, audit/ as organised into lane buckets that no longer exist, and engine/params/ as 'deletion lands in W7'. The deprecated/ row now records what SURVIVES and why -- the editorial-ledger archives are the BLOCKING citation gate's ED universe, and removing them would destroy the anti-fabrication check.
source: Fable-5 read-only review, 2026-08-05 ('keep it simple, don't build tools unnecessarily')

title: THE EVACUATION: 1,721 files removed, and the FORKED terminal status that let live citations survive it
description: Jordan: 'I don't really understand why we didn't just bulk move a whole bunch of stuff to fork, leave things dangling in main, and just resolve from there' -- then 'just fucking do it'. He was right. Three layers of reader-prediction machinery existed to FORECAST what a deletion would break; the W3 rehearsal answered it in ten minutes by doing it. Executed: 3,003 -> 1,282 tracked, evacuate set 1,721 -> 0. Recovery point c451bcb. UNBLOCKED BY: excising tools/compliance_check.py's orchestrator half (check_all / validate_commit / auto_fix / find_index_for / _lazy_import and the /home/claude sys.path insert). Its `import github_ops` was the LAST live reference from the non-deprecated tree into the retired orchestrator; the CI path never called any of it; removal cost ZERO live functionality. THE FORKED TERMINAL STATUS is the one piece of new mechanism and it was NOT optional: 25 live ledger entries cite audit units that were their EVIDENCE and are now at a fork ref. Every unresolvable reference was DEAD, so correct citations read as breakage in a blocking gate. A restructure_ledger row may now target FORK:<ref>, meaning legitimately absent with provenance at that ref. CRITICALLY it is NOT 'ignore missing' -- a reference with no row still fails -- because erasing that distinction would destroy the anti-fabrication property. A review named this as the single most likely thing to go wrong, so the control shipped WITH the status: tests/valoria/test_forked_status.py plants both cases, requires every FORK ref to be a real commit, and verifies the evacuated content is ACTUALLY present at that ref rather than trusting the row. GATES: 7 red -> 0. export_params_constants retired with its source from 5 wiring points; 8 completed one-shot .claude/wf_*.js retired with their subject (34 DEAD -> 0); ci_wf_harness_check taught that zero scripts is legitimate while still failing if the OWNER is missing; freshness_gate green by PRUNING canonical_sources (not --update, which would pin nothing for missing files and silently bless the deletion); currency_consistency_check taught that a tombstone line is not a head claim, line-locally so a genuinely stale head elsewhere still fails.

title: Plan step G7 EXECUTED: the repo root, the 9-lane roster and the token estimate collapse onto one owner in ci_common; the id_reservations row of the plan's own table is CORRECTED to nothing-to-do
description: Executes G7 of audit/2026-08-11-code-leanness/01_plan.md, promoted to the head of Track G by that document's section 8.4 because it is 140 of the 180 definitions the centralization directive targets and nothing gates it. tools/ci_common.py becomes the single import surface for tools/ (section 8.3), and tools/observability/obs_core.py RE-EXPORTS the dependency-free primitives from it rather than owning them. THE LAYERING DIRECTION IS FORCED, NOT CHOSEN: obs_core imports build_decisions, which requires PyYAML and sweeps the corpus at import time, while several stdlib-only BLOCKING gates (validate_ed_citations, currency_consistency_check, ci_workplan_pointer_check) need nothing from it but the 9-code tuple -- routing them through obs_core to read a constant would have made a stdlib gate depend on the observability tier. obs_core's heavier primitives (the ledger reader, the JS-bundle writer, STATUS_RE) are re-exported from ci_common LAZILY via PEP-562 module __getattr__, so `import ci_common` still pulls in neither obs_core nor PyYAML -- asserted in a subprocess by test_lazy_reexport_is_actually_lazy, without which the __getattr__ would be decorative and a plain top-level import would pass every other assertion. MEASURED WITH THE PLAN'S OWN INSTRUMENT (audit/2026-08-11-code-leanness/duplication_census.py), before -> after: ci_common adoption 11/118 -> 60/118; repo-root re-implementation 53 -> 24; 9-lane roster 9 -> 3; token estimation 6 -> 5. ZERO unmigrated repo-root definitions remain in tools/: the 24 residual detector hits are 12 in the tools/sim_harness/ cluster (promote-or-retire is HELD for Jordan), 7 in skills/*/scripts (outside the step's scope), and 5 irreducible bootstrap lines that anchor on their own module's directory rather than on the repo root. The roster's 3 and the token estimate's 5 residuals are all in atomizer/doc_index_gen/index_gen, which plan step G2 retires -- migrating a module scheduled for retirement would be work done twice. EXPECTED DELTA = NONE, AND IT IS ASSERTED RATHER THAN PREDICTED. Findings section 6 item 9 is explicit that every Track-G 'delta: none' claim is a prediction until its migration test establishes it. tests/valoria/test_ci_common_primitives.py (30 tests) recomputes each primitive THE WAY THE CALL SITES USED TO -- all four repo-root spellings transcribed verbatim from the migrated sources, the lane literal transcribed from all five modules that carried it, len(text)//4 parametrized -- and asserts the owner agrees. It is not self-consistency: it also anchors the root against `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` (the one check that could catch all fifteen spellings being wrong TOGETHER, which a transcription test cannot see by construction) and against CLAUDE.md section 4's prose lane table. Full suite 1803 passed / 23 skipped / 14 xfailed / 1 xpassed, plus valoria_local --staged all gates passed, and every migrated tool smoke-run for import-level breakage (0 failures). ONE CORRECTION TO THE PLAN, filed rather than silently skipped (section 0.1 point 3). The plan's section 8.1 table lists 'id_reservations read | 8 | 1 | removed 7'. Executing it found NOTHING TO COLLAPSE: measured across the whole tree, ZERO modules load references/id_reservations.yaml. The census's detector for that row is the bare string `id_reservations`, so its 8 are MENTIONS -- six prose comments, one ci_register_size_check size-cap row keyed by path string, one build_decisions source tuple. ci_common therefore deliberately ships NO reader for it: adding one would have been an abstraction with no caller, which is exactly the build-then-disconnect defect ED-IN-0149 named and the consolidation sweep ranked. The falsifier is test_no_module_actually_loads_id_reservations, which fails the moment a real loader appears -- that being the correct moment to give the primitive an owner. AND THE INSTRUMENT COUNTED ITSELF, AGAIN. That test's first run failed on two files: itself (its source carries `id_reservations` beside `safe_load` as the pattern it searches for) and ci_common.py (whose comment quotes the grep command). That is findings section 2.4 verbatim, reproduced by the test written to guard the finding one section away from where the trap is documented. Self-exclusion added and recorded in the test's own docstring rather than quietly patched. title: Plan step G8 EXECUTED: one owner for the `## Status:` reader — and three corrections to the finding it executes, including that one of the five diverging parsers does not exist
description: Executes G8 of audit/2026-08-11-code-leanness/01_plan.md, the ONE intended behaviour change in Track G. STATUS_RE, first_status and the new doc_status move to tools/ci_common.py (same layering rule as G7 -- a dependency-free regex read by a stdlib-only gate belongs below the observability tier), and tools/observability/obs_core.py re-exports them, so every existing obs_core consumer is byte-identical. Three live readers migrated: build_identifier_census.doc_status, ci_generation_consistency.status_of, build_incompleteness's fused status+vocabulary regex (now STATUS_RE composed with NONCURRENT_VOCAB). THREE CORRECTIONS TO FINDING 1.3a, each measured. (1) THERE ARE FOUR LIVE READERS, NOT FIVE. The table attributes `^#{1,3}\\s*Status:` to dashboard_data. That attribute DOES NOT EXIST -- dashboard_data.py:695 calls obs_core.first_status and has since obs_core was built. The pattern survives only in obs_core's own HISTORICAL COMMENT recording the regex it replaced; the census transcribed a comment describing a past state as a present one. Every 'invisible to: dashboard_data' cell in the disputed table is therefore wrong -- dashboard_data sees exactly what the canonical owner sees. (2) THE DELTA IS ONE-SIDED, NOT TWO-SIDED. 1.3a predicted collapsing would 'add documents to two parsers' view and can remove them from a third's'. Measured: ci_generation_consistency's regex was ALREADY EQUIVALENT to the owner (206 docs, 0 gained, 0 lost -- it never diverged), build_incompleteness composes with 0 gained and 0 lost in its own scope (25 -> 25), and ONLY build_identifier_census moves, at +3 / -1. Nothing is removed from anyone. (3) THE DIVERGENCE THAT MATTERED WAS THE WINDOW, NOT THE REGEX. The three readers scan 12 lines / 80 lines / the whole document, and 1.3a compared their regexes by running all five over WHOLE documents -- which is how none of them is used. Over a whole document the canonical pattern matches a schema TEMPLATE (`  status : IN_FORCE | VETOED | SUPERSEDED`) and a table LEGEND (`## Status: NOT STARTED / IN PROGRESS / COMPLETE`). ci_common.STATUS_HEAD_LINES = 80 is now a named constant chosen BY MEASUREMENT against the SUPERSEDED classification that actually consumes it: 12 lines flips 2 (two genuinely-superseded docs stop being recognised), 40 flips 0, 80 flips 0, whole-document flips 1 (a schema template read as a status). 40 and 80 agreeing is the stability the choice rests on. THE DISPUTED SEVEN, FULLY PARTITIONED: all seven are ONE cause -- build_identifier_census's `^##\\s*Status:` required EXACTLY TWO HASHES -- and they split 3 + 2 + 2. THREE are real statuses now visible (engine/sim_reference_CONVENTIONS.md, references/restructure_ledger.md, systems/combat/combat_engine_v1/README.md). TWO are whole-document FALSE POSITIVES the head window correctly refuses (skills/valoria-simulator/SKILL.md, audit/2026-08-06-social-contest-three-lens-audit/sources/03_consolidation.md). TWO ARE DOCUMENT DEFECTS NO REGEX CAN FIX and are LEFT OPEN AND NAMED: workplans/valoria_master_workplan_v6.md -- THE LIVE STEERING SURFACE -- carries no conventional Status line at all (its currency is stated mid-sentence as '2026-07-05 - status: CANON — RATIFIED'), and systems/ui/valoria_ui_ux_v4.md wraps its in bold (`**Status:**`). Those are content fixes in the workplans and UI lanes; an infrastructure step must not paper over them by loosening the owner, so the test asserts they are STILL invisible and fails when either is fixed. ONE MECHANISM NEARLY LOST, CAUGHT BY THE TWO-SIDED REQUIREMENT. The first build_incompleteness helper returned at the FIRST Status line -- obviously right, and wrong: systems/factions/faction_canon_v30.md carries '## Status: CANONICAL' on line 6 and '## Status: PROVISIONAL — pending ratification.' on line 7, and the fused regex it replaced used re.M search, skipping line 6 and matching line 7. Stopping at the first line dropped that document from the incompleteness feed. This is exactly the silent shrink the plan required a two-sided test to catch, and the one-sided version of the test would have passed. The contradictory Status pair is itself a live FA-lane document defect, reported by the feed rather than fixed here. MEASURED-BY: tests/valoria/test_status_reader_one_owner.py -- 19 passed; asserts each reader's gain AND loss sets by name, the 3+2+2 partition of the disputed seven summing to 7, zero SUPERSEDED reclassifications, the 40/80 window stability with both failing endpoints, and that exactly ONE compiled Status regex remains in the whole tooling tier. MEASURED-BY: audit/2026-08-11-code-leanness/duplication_census.py -- the five-reader disagreement table. Full suite 1822 passed / 23 skipped / 14 xfailed / 1 xpassed.

title: ADVERSARIAL PASS on this session's own G7/G8/G1/G2 work: five claims REFUTED, all five fixed — including ci_common shipping three abstractions with no caller, one commit after refusing a fourth for exactly that reason
description: An independent read-only valoria-critic pass (CLAUDE.md section 10 relay: OUTPUT only, no reasoning, Read/Grep/Glob) attacked this session's G7/G8/G1/G2 claims and REFUTED FIVE. All five fixed, none argued away. (1) SELF-CONTRADICTION IN ONE FILE: ci_common labelled the id regexes and load_yaml/load_register 'ONE OWNER' with ZERO callers -- the copies were all still live, including two in ci_vetting_check, a BLOCKING gate not importing ci_common -- fifty lines below the same file refusing read_id_reservations() for exactly that reason. CLAUDE.md section 8's named anti-pattern, re-earned one commit after section 2.3 withdrew it against pathres. FIXED: load_register and six speculative id variants DELETED; PP_ID_PAT kept and its 3 call sites migrated (delta-none proven against the live patch register); load_yaml gained 12 call sites and its docstring now states the honest residual (52 bare yaml.safe_load remain) in pathres's style. (2) 'ZERO unmigrated repo-root definitions remain in tools/' WAS FALSE -- five live sites remained, four in modules whose SIBLINGS were migrated. All five migrated. (3) NO RECURRENCE GUARD for G7's five primitives while G8 shipped one for STATUS_RE (section 0.1 point 5). Five guards added; one of them found and condemned refutation 1's residue on its first run. (4) THE WINDOW WAS NOT SINGLE-OWNED and STATUS_HEAD_LINES=80's stated justification was FALSE -- dashboard_data read f.read(4000), a per-caller CHARACTER literal, so four windows still existed. Fixed; measured delta 114 -> 114, i.e. latent not firing. (5) A BLOCKING GATE EDITED WITH NO TEST -- ci_co_file_checker has none anywhere, violating the plan's second governing rule. Added test_co_file_rules.py (8 tests) asserting each surviving rule can still FAIL, not merely run; its tombstone corrected for overclaiming that six code->artifact gates 'now carry' a doc->doc rule and were 'strictly stronger' (all six PRE-EXISTED; nothing was transferred; the real reason is that Rule 4's SUBJECT left the tree). AND THE SUITE CAUGHT WHAT THE CRITIC DID NOT: load_yaml defaulted to None, so a migrated bare open() -- which RAISES -- began SILENTLY absorbing a missing input. 12 tests red, five on that, including test_engine_atlas::test_missing_input_is_reported_not_silently_absorbed, a guard written for this defect class. Fixed with a sentinel, not a looser test: load_yaml(p) raises exactly as before; forgiving mode is opt-in. NOT FIXED, RECORDED: re-measuring dead policy rows by 'matches zero files' rather than path prefix gives 25, not the 6 the critic found. NOT mass-deleted -- most are ANTICIPATORY by the same rule that kept editorial_ledger_go.jsonl. That triage IS plan step G5's meta-guard. Also: dashboard_data:696's proposals/ branch is unreachable, and ci_checks_registry.yaml:61 describes a fourth co-file rule that does not exist. title: THREE-LENS adversarial review of this branch: 9 defects found, 3 of them by independent rediscovery; all fixed, and 20 mutants now killed where 0 had been run
description: Three independent read-only valoria-critic passes (CLAUDE.md section 10 relay -- OUTPUT only, no reasoning, Read/Grep/Glob) with disjoint lenses: correctness/logic, repo compliance/applicability, data shaping/value. Plus my own runtime verification, which the critics could not do. THE STRONGEST SIGNAL: THREE PASSES INDEPENDENTLY FOUND THE SAME DEFECT. test_every_ci_common_primitive_has_a_caller -- the guard written to catch the build-then-disconnect defect ED-IN-0164 had just caught -- was VACUOUS for every def-defined export. Its internal-use clause was owner_src.split(f'{name} =',1)[-1], and a function has no 'name =' in the source, so split returned the WHOLE FILE and the regex matched the function's own def line. load_yaml, doc_status, tokens, read_text and every get_* helper could have had zero callers and passed. Section 10 ranks by independent rediscovery only when blind spots DIFFER; here they did. REBUILT on AST (is the name LOADED outside its own definition?) and mutation-verified against its own incident class: re-adding a callerless load_register is now KILLED. MUTATION VERIFICATION, THE COMPLIANCE GAP THE REVIEW NAMED. This repo's standard for a guard is mutation testing (test_wf_harness 13/13, test_flow_skeletons 8/8, test_j2_mass_battle_seam). The branch had shipped ~1,100 lines of new test claiming NONE. 20 mutants were then written and run: 20/20 KILLED, covering the repo root, the lane roster, the token denominator, REPO_PATH decoupling, load_yaml's silent-absorb, STATUS_RE narrowing, both window endpoints, re-derivation, a second roster literal, a new inline //4, a new bare yaml.safe_load, a second Status regex, first-line-wins in build_incompleteness, the two-hash regex, the provenance archive, the rationale copy-paste, the pointer regrowth, and both co-file mutations. SEVEN FURTHER DEFECTS, EACH VERIFIED WITH BASH BEFORE FIXING. (1) A GATE I CAUSED TO SHRINK: ci_claim_provenance_check's LEDGERS named only the LIVE lane files, so ARCHIVING an entry removed its measured claims from scope forever -- and archiving is routine under the 50k cap. Archiving ED-IN-0160/0161 moved this branch's own headline numbers out of scope; the gate's count fell 23 -> 22 between main and HEAD while reporting green. Measured fix: scope 22 -> 47 across 4 ledgers, STILL GREEN -- the coverage was free and had never been claimed. (2) THE DEAD-SCOPE SWEEP MANUFACTURED A DEAD ROW: it 'repointed' the designs/audit skip row to audit/2026-07-08-attribute-value-coherence-audit/..., which does NOT exist -- restructure_ledger.md:1257-1258 records BOTH spellings as FORK:c451bcb. Against the entry's own rule ('an absent path is dead only if its subject was RETIRED') the correct disposition was deletion. Now deleted. (3) THE ROSTER CLAIM '9 -> 3' WAS WRONG ON CONCEPT: the census matched the TUPLE spelling, so it never saw two DICT enumerations (build_decisions.LANE_NAMES, dashboard_data.LANE_NAMES) -- which had ALREADY DIVERGED ('Settlements' vs 'settlement / territory'; 'Faction actions' vs 'faction / political'), CLAUDE.md section 8's same-name-divergent-value class live in the tree. Both now derive their KEYS from the owner (display strings stay per-surface deliberately) with a totality guard. (4) A FIFTH WINDOW SURVIVED: build_proposals._doc_head kept the identical 4,000-CHARACTER literal, so PROPOSALS.md and the dashboard card -- which dashboard_data asserts 'call the same core, so they agree' -- measurably did not. Routed through STATUS_HEAD_LINES; measured delta 124 -> 124, latent not firing. (5) RULE 1 CARRIED THE SAME DEAD SCOPE AS RULE 4: '(?:designs|systems)/' -- half-dead since 2026-07-19, in the file the dead-scope sweep edited and read. Removed. (6) test_rules_1_to_3_can_still_FAIL grepped for 'violations.append' while claiming in its docstring to construct a changeset -- and Rule 4 was retired for CONTAINING that string while unreachable. REWRITTEN to build a real git repo, stage a design-doc change without its co-file, and require rc=1, with a co-changed control; both mutations killed. (7) Dead REPO='jordanelias/ttrpg' slug (a THIRD meaning of REPO) and a dead module-level import yaml in a stdlib-only blocking gate -- the latter defeating ci_common's lazy-import rationale at the exact site that motivated it. Both removed. AND THE LEANNESS PROGRAMME HAD ITSELF DUPLICATED: measuring the branch's own delta showed tools/ +2,384/-896 lines against a NON-COMMENT delta of only +406/-226 -- because a 5-line bootstrap rationale had been copy-pasted into 54 files, 242 comment lines, the exact defect class the step was executing against. Collapsed to a 3-line pointer with the explanation living once in ci_common's docstring; 80 lines removed and two guards added (no long-form copies; the pointer may not regrow). CONTINUITY SURFACES RECONCILED, the compliance-critical finding: ED-IN-0163 is needs_jordan:true and appeared in NEITHER CURRENT.md's stamp NOR HANDOFF_IN.md, while HANDOFF_IN said 'Next in the plan: G2' -- work already landed. A held Jordan ruling invisible to both currency surfaces is ED-1094's failure mode reconstituted. The plan of record's own Status line still read 'nothing executed'. All three corrected. NOT FIXED, RECORDED: dashboard_data's proposals/ branch is unreachable under its systems/** glob (its note advertises coverage it lacks); build_incompleteness narrowed #{0,4} to #{0,3} with no doc currently using four hashes, so the 'delta none' rests on an unasserted corpus property; ci_checks_registry:61 still describes a phantom fourth co-file rule; 25 zero-match policy rows await plan step G5's triage. title: ED-IN-0162 closed: the stale census is regenerated AND gated -- and the gate it was going to be given could not see the file the finding names first
description: EXECUTES the fix ED-IN-0162 filed and #305 deliberately deferred ('fix lands next, separately', so a 9,773-line regeneration would not bury a review). CONFIRMED THE FINDING BEFORE ACTING ON IT, against the tree rather than the ledger: the committed systems/combat/_identifier_census.yaml listed SEVEN docs -- combat_design_v1.md, combat_design_v1_index.md, combat_v30.md, combat_v30_index.md, combat_v30_infill.md among them, all deleted by the 2026-08-08 personal-combat 5->1 consolidation -- and knew nothing of combat_reference_v1.md or the 2026-08-10 combat_flow_skeleton_v1.md. A generated inventory of what each subsystem NAMES, computed over a doc list containing deleted files, feeding references/glossary/ which IS freshness-gated. THE TOOL'S OWN --check WAS INCAPABLE OF CATCHING IT. main() returned on the --check branch BEFORE the roll-up write, so references/identifier_census.json -- the artifact ED-IN-0162 names first -- was the one file --check never compared. Wiring the pre-existing --check into a gate, which is exactly what the finding prescribed, would have shipped an assertion incapable of observing the failure it excludes (CLAUDE.md 0.1 point 2). Fixed in the tool: the roll-up is compared on full runs, and NOT on --subsystem X runs, because a scoped run computes one row and would report drift that is an artifact of the flag. MEASURED, NOT PREDICTED: 15 subsystems drifted (not the 16 ED-IN-0162 stated -- there are 15 census files and 15 subsystem folders; corrected here), the roll-up changed 61 lines by git numstat (the committed file is 99 lines; "61 of its 61" as first published described the diff, not the file), and the glossary went 1,537 -> 2,065 terms once rebuilt from the fresh census. FALSIFIER, per 0.1 point 3: tests/valoria/test_identifier_census.py, whose test_check_sees_a_corrupted_rollup is the mutation the PRE-FIX code survives. Mutation-verified 2/2 -- M1 (the pre-fix early return) is killed by all three roll-up checks, M2 (scoped guard removed) by the scoped-silence check. NO WORKING-TREE MUTATION in those tests: test_engine_atlas can plant a probe folder safely because nothing else reads zz_atlas_probe, but corrupting references/identifier_census.json in place would be read concurrently by test_build_glossary under -n auto, which is the C6 race. The two-sided tests build a fake repo in tmp_path and monkeypatch the module REPO instead. MEASURED-BY: tools/build_identifier_census.py (--check reports the drifted files; a full run prints the 15-subsystem roll-up and the BUILT/UNRESOLVED totals) and tools/observability/build_glossary.py (prints the term count: 2,065). Both re-runnable from a clean checkout; the 1,537 figure is the pre-regeneration count recorded in ED-IN-0162. RECORDED, NOT FIXED — A POLICY GAP THE REGENERATION SURFACED. Bringing the census current took compliance_check from 48 warnings to 59, and all 11 new ones are size_exceeded on GENERATED files: 7 systems/*/_identifier_census.yaml and 4 references/glossary/GLOSSARY_*.md. Zero errors, nothing regressed, and the diff against origin/main shows no warning disappeared. But the atomization size caps apply to generated artifacts where THE DOCUMENTED REMEDY DOES NOT EXIST: you cannot split a file the generator overwrites on its next run, and the 2026-07-26 sequential-parts ruling is about authored documents. The honest dispositions are a generated-file rule in references/atomization_rules.yaml or teaching the two generators to chunk their output; both are larger than this step and neither is load-bearing on it (CLAUDE.md 0.1 point 5 -- widening scope has a real cost, and the last time this session did it the cost was measured). Filed for plan step G6, which is the size-cap step and already owns the question of which caps apply where.

title: Plan step G3: two tools that cannot fail leave the blocking tier, and the valoria_hooks ghost tier is deleted -- including a dead branch inside a blocking gate
description: EXECUTES plan step G3 (audit/2026-08-11-code-leanness/01_plan.md), covering findings 1.9 and 1.10. 1.9 -- ci_supersession_check.py documents 'ALWAYS return 0 (WARN-ONLY)' at :66 and every return in its main() is 0; ci_audit_registry_check.py's own registry row says 'Always exits 0 by design'. Both sat in validators, the BLOCKING job, so two of its nineteen entries misreported what blocks a merge. Moved to validators-report with the registry ci_job rows flipped in the SAME commit, because broken_dependency_checker joins the two directions and reds if they disagree. NOT A RELAXATION, and this is the part worth recording: valoria_local.py:162,172 ALREADY ran both report-only, so the two tiers had disagreed for months and the stricter-LOOKING one was the wrong one. CI caught up to local. THE GUARD IS THE DELIVERABLE, NOT THE MOVE (0.1 point 5). test_no_blocking_validator_is_incapable_of_failing reds if a third always-exit-0 tool enters the blocking job. It needs NO allowlist: measured at write time with a CORRECTED instrument (see ED-IN-0169): 20 of 20 blocking tools can exit non-zero and all 5 that cannot are in validators-report. The figures first published were 17 and 6, both wrong -- 17 counted only the validators job and missed ci_golden_modes_check/compliance_check/review_core in other blocking jobs, and 6 came from a detector that misclassified ci_module_shape_check and ci_workplan_pointer_check, so the invariant holds with zero exceptions. 1.10 -- valoria_hooks.py lived ONLY at deprecated/skills/valoria-orchestrator/scripts/ and was removed by the 2026-08-05 evacuation (cadf9c7). It left behind: the level-4 rung of the enforcement ladder, a paired_hook field definition, a 19-entry in_session_hooks section, and 3 rows claiming level 4 while being report-only CI tools. 124 ghost lines -- 89 for the in_session_hooks section plus 35 paired_hook lines -- and ONE code consumer, not zero -- broken_dependency_checker check (d) read the paired_hook field, which this very entry says two sentences later; the in_session_hooks SECTION had zero consumers and the aggregate wrongly extended that to the field; the file itself goes 479 -> 373, a NET 106, because ~18 lines of tombstone were added back. Deleted under the rule ED-IN-0163 had to state for the OPPOSITE case: an absent path is dead only if its SUBJECT was retired, never merely because it is absent -- and here the subject was retired deliberately. WORSE THAN DEAD PROSE, AND THE FINDING DID NOT SAY SO: broken_dependency_checker's check (d) verified those paired_hooks, and since the evacuation it had done nothing except os.walk the ENTIRE REPO on every run of a blocking gate to rediscover the file was gone, then append an ERROR line saying it had skipped. The same G1 defect class this plan excised from compliance_check.py one commit earlier. Numbering deliberately left as 1/2/3/5 with the gap visible; renumbering 5 to 4 would silently rewrite the meaning of every existing level: 5 row. CORRECTION, self-found before commit and recorded rather than quietly patched: this entry first said "123 lines", a net figure read off a MID-EDIT run and reported as though it were the ghost surface. It had already propagated to CURRENT.md and HANDOFF_IN before the adversarial pass caught it; all three are corrected. The measured figures are 479 -> 373 committed (net 106), ghost removal 124. Small, and worth recording anyway: ED-PC-0040 exists precisely because three consecutive batches shipped confident numbers that measurement later contradicted, and the failure mode is never the size of the error. MEASURED-BY: tests/valoria/test_blocking_tier_is_honest.py reproduces the 20/20-can-fail and 5-report-only partition from the live workflow via tools/ci_gate_coverage.py; the line counts are `git show ed7d0fd~1:references/ci_checks_registry.yaml | wc -l` (479) against `wc -l references/ci_checks_registry.yaml` (373), and the 89/35 split is `git show ed7d0fd~1:references/ci_checks_registry.yaml | grep -c "^[ ]*paired_hook:"` (35 keys, of which 6 non-empty) plus the in_session_hooks section span. Instrument for the tier claim: tools/ci_gate_coverage.py.

title: A STALE generated artifact feeds a FRESHNESS-GATED one: identifier_census has no gate of any kind, and references/glossary/ is built from it
description: Found while executing plan step G8, outside its scope, filed rather than fixed in that commit. references/identifier_census.json and the 16 systems/*/_identifier_census.yaml files were last generated 2026-08-04 (commit e3eab09). The documents they index changed on 2026-08-08 (ED-PC-0056 consolidated the five personal-combat docs into one, so the census still lists combat_design_v1.md, combat_v30.md, combat_v30_index.md and combat_v30_infill.md as live) and on 2026-08-10 (ED-IN-0152 added 15 flow skeletons, none of which the census knows about). Regenerating produces a 9,773-line diff across 16 files. NOTHING GATES IT: no CI job invokes build_identifier_census, it is absent from tools/valoria_local.py, and no test runs a --check or byte-compares committed output against a fresh build. WHY THIS IS SHARPER THAN THE ALREADY-FILED INSTANCES. ED-IN-0158's adversarial pass established that build_glossary / build_engine_atlas / build_contract_index have zero schedulers but ARE guarded by --check/byte-compare tests in the blocking suite, and concluded that a freshness gate BEATS a scheduled regenerator because it fails the PR that caused the staleness. references/glossary/ is one of those three -- and identifier_census is one of its FIVE SOURCES (1,243 of the glossary's 1,537 terms). So the guarded artifact is built from an unguarded one: the glossary's --check can only prove the glossary matches its inputs, never that its inputs match the tree. The gate is real and its coverage stops one layer short. MEASURED-BY: git log -1 -- references/identifier_census.json gives 2026-08-04 (e3eab09), while git log -1 -- systems/combat/combat_reference_v1.md gives 2026-08-08 (6bc0828). MEASURED-BY: python tools/build_identifier_census.py followed by git diff --stat gives 16 files changed, 9,773 insertions, 273 deletions on a tree with no source edits of its own.

title: Plan step G9: being compiled stops counting as being invoked -- orphans 7 -> 11, and my first implementation reproduced the exact trap a test one file away already names
description: EXECUTES plan step G9, both halves in one commit as the plan requires. HALF A: the syntax-check job was a hand-maintained py_compile list naming 32 of the 108 .py under tools/, so 76 tools -- all of tools/observability/ and tools/sim_harness/ among them -- could carry a syntax error into main past a gate whose name says otherwise. Globbed via find|xargs rather than tools/*.py, because the shell glob does not descend into the subdirectories that are half the uncovered set; py_compile kept as the literal mechanism because ci_gate_coverage keys its compile-only job classification on that token. Verified all 108 compile before switching. HALF B: invoked_by tags a tool ci:<workflow> when its basename appears anywhere in the workflow text, so being in the compile list counted as being invoked. MEASURED: 6 tools had no other invoker-surface mention, of which 4 change orphan status (atomizer, doc_index_gen, index_gen, valoria_rename -- exactly the four 2.2 named; ci_common and names are imported elsewhere so their status does not move). Result: orphans 7 -> 11, prune candidates 0 -> 2 (doc_index_gen, index_gen). BOTH HALVES, AND THE DELTA CLAIM HAS A CONTROL (0.1 point 4). Measured all four combinations: either half alone produces the same 4 flips today, so half B's measured delta is ZERO and saying otherwise would be a claim without a control. Its job is the recurrence case, and that case was executed rather than argued -- test_naming_every_tool_in_the_compile_gate_does_not_zero_the_census simulates the obvious 'fix' of naming all 108 tools and shows it re-tags 4/4 without the strip and 0/4 with it. MY FIRST IMPLEMENTATION WAS WRONG AND THE INSTRUMENT CAUGHT IT, NOT ME. strip_compile_only_steps was one multiline regex; it swallowed the ENTIRE validators-report job, because that job's run block mentions py_compile INSIDE A COMMENT ('no workflow invokes valoria_local at all (only py_compile on it)'). It reported 13 orphans and 2 prune candidates, of which mechanics_index_gen and ci_workplan_pointer_check were FALSE -- both are live validators in that job. That is test_gate_coverage.py::test_a_comment_mentioning_py_compile_does_not_zero_a_jobs_command_list, reproduced one file away from the test that names it, which is the ED-IN-0161 'the instrument counted itself' shape again. Rewritten as an indentation-aware line scanner with an explicit _INVOKES guard (a step that also invokes a tool is never compile-only, whatever its comments say), and a second over-reach was then found and fixed by the same route: skipping comment lines when locating the step end made it swallow the 21-line banner introducing the next job. Final strip removed 7 lines (6 of step plus its blank separator); "exactly 6" as first published was wrong. The over-reach direction is now tested at least as hard as the under-reach one. MEASURED-BY: tools/build_apparatus_registry.py --dry-run prints "orphaned(no importer/invoker)=N prune_candidates=M" — 7/0 on origin/main, 11/2 here — and audit/2026-08-11-code-leanness/duplication_census.py for the adoption/re-implementation figures. The 32-of-108 compile coverage is reproduced by `find tools -name "*.py" -not -path "*/__pycache__/*" | wc -l` against the pre-G9 py_compile list at git show ed7d0fd~1:.github/workflows/valoria-ci.yml. The four flipped tools are reproduced by tests/valoria/test_compile_is_not_invocation.py.

title: Degree-vocabulary census: the ruling is 7 decisions, not 16 -- and 8 of 11 sites need no ruling at all
description: Jordan asked for the measurement that prices the held degree/vocabulary ruling (#0, which gates #1 and #2). Built and ran audit/2026-08-12-degree-vocabulary-census/degree_census.py. METHOD: every ladder that is a function of (net, ob) is evaluated over 600 integer cells + 890 quarter-step cells, output normalised to an ORDINAL BAND so spelling is stripped entirely; ladders with identical band surfaces are ONE decision however many ways they are spelled. The functions are IMPORTED, not transcribed -- re-typing them would have measured my copy and agreed with itself (the ED-IN-0132 F1 defect). RESULT: 11 code sites -> 8 distinct ladders -> SEVEN equivalence classes. MECHANICALLY MERGEABLE WITH NO RULING (8 of 11 sites): the three inline ob+3 copies (mass_seizure:264, collective:166, knots:226) are identical to threadwork/operations:134; the two mass-battle ladders (resolution:89 with _DEGREE_EPS, massbattle:640 without) are identical on all 1,490 cells; and four of the audit's 16 'producers' (echo_transport:187, parliamentary_bridge:100, scene_dispatch:260/:334) are TRANSLATORS carrying no band boundaries at all. GENUINELY NEEDS A RULING, priced: faction_action:97 diverges from canon on 670/1490 cells (45.0%) -- the largest by far, and structural rather than a threshold choice, because its _degree takes only net with ob pre-subtracted at :520, making the net==0 -> Partial branch the s==ob dead zone #304 filed as item #1. Then opposing:87 at 37.6%, additive ob+3 at 15.3%, combat/core:57 at 5.6% (fractional only), the skill fork at 3.3%, and mass battle vs canon at 0.6% -- those 9 cells being ENTIRELY the ob>=20 canon exception. THE INSTRUMENT'S FIRST RUN WAS WRONG AND IS RECORDED AS SUCH: it reported 6 classes on the integer domain, grouping combat/core:57 with the mass-battle pair, because a -0.5 continuity correction is INVISIBLE at integer nets -- the one domain a continuous resolver is never evaluated on. Quarter steps split the class. A class computed on the wrong domain is a merge recommendation that silently changes behaviour, which is the exact defect the census exists to prevent, reproduced by the census on its own first run; it now evaluates both domains and warns when they disagree. TWO EXPLICIT NON-CLAIMS: the epsilon result does NOT refute ED-MB-0051 (its justification is accumulated float error, which a quarter-step grid cannot produce, so this census is structurally unable to observe the case it was written for); and every cell is weighted equally, so this prices SURFACE, not REACHABILITY -- ranking by how often a band actually fires still needs plan T4, which remains unrun. sigma_leverage:284 excluded by design (pool-aware, shares no domain, and is the most-pinned ladder in the repo at 1,758 golden rows).

title: The alias plan's foundation EXECUTED, not read -- confirmed, plus the anti-fabrication finding a control produced and the plan could not have
description: audit/2026-08-12-alias-index-consolidation/00_plan.md rests its whole sequencing argument on 'the same row resolves five different ways, two of them inside BLOCKING gates' -- a claim derived by READING five modules, never by running them. The plan says so itself and names running it as the first executable step because everything else depends on it. This is that step. It changes no parser and consolidates nothing. CONFIRMED: one 1-hop FORK row (engine/params/core.md) yields 5 distinct verdicts across 6 consumers -- FORKED (pathres), INFO-EVACUATED (broken_dependency_checker), DEAD (ci_claude_workflow_paths, a BLOCKING gate), missing (vector_audit, workbench), nonexistent (gen_audit). The hop-count claim reproduces exactly (the real 2-hop chain params/ -> engine/params/ -> FORK is FORKED under pathres's chained resolution and BROKEN under bdc's single-hop), as does the two-payload-shapes claim (bare FORK:<ref> for an exact row, FORK:<ref>:<path> for a prefix row, from one function). THE FINDING THE PLAN DOES NOT HAVE, AND WHAT PRODUCED IT. The plan asks 'do the consumers disagree about a FORK row'. The question that matters is the one tests/valoria/test_forked_status.py calls 'the repo's anti-fabrication property': a path that left deliberately must not look like a path that never existed. That file proves it for ONE consumer. So every probe here also runs a CONTROL -- a path with no ledger row at all. Result: the distinction survives in 5 of 18 (consumer x fork-row) pairs. Four consumers collapse it on EVERY row; a fifth collapses it conditionally; only pathres preserves it throughout. The plan states 'three of five consumers collapse exactly that distinction' -- measured against a control it is four of six outright plus one conditional, and the conditional one is a blocking gate. PER-PAIR, NOT PER-CONSUMER, AND THAT IS THE PART WORTH CARRYING. The first version of the instrument tracked a set of CONSUMER NAMES, on the natural assumption that a consumer either understands FORK: or does not. broken_dependency_checker refutes it: INFO-EVACUATED for a 1-hop row, BROKEN for a 2-hop chain -- and BROKEN is exactly what a fabricated path returns. Its anti-fabrication property is CONDITIONAL ON HOP COUNT, and a per-consumer roster would have had to record it as wholly safe or wholly broken, both false. The granularity of a measurement is not a presentation choice; it decides which findings are expressible. TWO CORRECTIONS TO MY OWN WORK, recorded because they are the method rather than an aside: (1) THE INSTRUMENT WAS WRONG BEFORE THE PLAN WAS -- the first probe modelled bdc._resolve_remap() as the decision and reported params/core.md as 'mapped', contradicting the plan's BROKEN prediction; the plan was right and the helper is not the decision (the caller at bdc:217-227 tests all_files membership first). A harness that models a helper instead of a decision measures its own model. (2) I reported 'only pathres and bdc preserve the distinction' before running the strict per-pair comparison; under it that is too generous to bdc. NOT A CONFORMANCE GATE, DELIBERATELY: failing on today's 13 collapsed pairs would red every unrelated PR immediately, which is the reds-on-day-one mistake ED-IN-0112 already paid for. The ratchet pins the 5 pairs that WORK and fails only when one stops working; Phase A2 grows it. Nothing here pre-empts Phase A1's five semantics, which stay HELD for Jordan. MEASURED-BY: audit/2026-08-13-fork-divergence-harness/fork_divergence.py -- re-runnable, with --check as the ratchet; tests/valoria/test_fork_divergence.py carries the positive control (plants a regression, requires the comparison to report exactly it), a not-vacuous floor on the baseline, and a coverage assertion so a silent import failure inside probe_all cannot read as agreement.

title: JORDAN RULING 2026-08-13: there is no deprecated/ conflict -- I manufactured it from two coined words, and the real defect is that vocabulary does not survive a session boundary
description: Jordan, verbatim: 'The completed evacuation *is* the retirement of all those files that were live prior to the evacuation. All future retirements, then, are joining already-retired items. There is no contradiction or conflict.' This settles the item ED-IN-0177 raised and PR #307 held. There was no conflict: 'evacuate' is not a deletion queue, it means move it out of main and keep it at a named ref, which is precisely the treatment a retired file should get. New retirements joining old ones is the policy working, not two policies colliding. HOW I PRODUCED A FALSE BLOCKER. The code says 'evacuate'; the prose says 'retirement'. NEITHER IS STANDARD SOFTWARE USAGE -- both were coined in this repo for this operation ('deprecate' is the real term of art and means something else again: still shipped, discouraged). I read the gap between two invented labels as evidence of a gap in the world, and escalated it into a held disposition across three surfaces and two PR bodies. JORDAN'S FRAMING IS SHARPER THAN MINE, and it generalises: 'Claude is not a human who has context between sessions... every session will need to reinterpret vocabulary used for a particular purpose in another session, and that can create compounding issues since the particular use of vocabulary isn't carried over and consequently causes the word to be misinterpreted going forward.' That is this incident exactly, observed live -- 'evacuate' was coined in an earlier session, I read it cold, inferred a meaning its author never held, and built work on the inference. The consequence for how this repo should be written: A COINED TERM IS A POINTER TO CONTEXT THAT DOES NOT SURVIVE. Plain words degrade gracefully because ordinary usage re-supplies the meaning; a coined word has no fallback, so each session re-derives it and the derivations drift. Simplicity is not a style preference here, it is the only form of definition that survives a context reset. THE ADJACENT WORRY WAS ALSO EMPTY, and checking beat reasoning for the third time this session: the load-bearing editorial-ledger archives are NOT swept into the evacuate bucket -- deprecated/archives/editorial* and deprecated/canon/ match R-RELOCATE ABOVE R-DEPRECATED and classify 'relocate', so the anti-fabrication universe is protected by rule ORDER. Two lines of classify() would have shown the mechanism was coherent before I wrote a word about it. MEASURED, to answer Jordan's follow-up question with evidence rather than opinion: 32 distinct process terms are in circulation across roughly 26,000 uses (disposition 4,894; ratif* 3,396; stub 2,141; consolidat* 2,046; collapse 1,722; demot* 1,686; retire 1,547; supersed* 1,530; evacuat* 632; and 23 more). NONE of the six existing vocabulary registries governs any of them: censured_vocabulary.yaml, synonym_registry.yaml and definitions/definitions.yaml each return ZERO for the four largest. Every registry in the tree governs DESIGN/WORLD vocabulary; PROCESS vocabulary is entirely ungoverned, which is why the term that caused this had nothing anchoring it. MEASURED-BY: tools/evacuation_plan.py -- `classify('deprecated/archives/editorials/editorial_ledger_archive_001_200.yaml')` returns ('relocate', 'R-RELOCATE', ...) while `classify('deprecated/tools/atomizer.py')` returns ('evacuate', 'R-DEPRECATED', ...), which is the two-line check that dissolves both the claimed conflict and the archive worry; the 32-term census is a reproducible grep over .md/.py/.yaml/.jsonl excluding deprecated/.

title: Waves 4+5: the single-owner bypass guard (14 real, measured), and TWO generated artifacts that nothing refreshed -- one visibly stale, one fresh only by luck [SUPERSEDED IN PART -- see the corrections at the end of this description]
description: WAVE 4 -- THE DUPLICATION GUARDRAIL, keyed on the owned resource rather than on the phrase. The obvious build greps for modules that claim ownership and checks whether others honour it; that would be this programme's signature defect one level up, since a phrase in a comment is not the property -- tools/pathres.py declared itself 'THE path-reference owner' for months while four other modules parsed the same file, and the declaration is exactly what stopped readers from checking. So the question asked is factual: does this module build a path to the registry itself? AND IT PARSES RATHER THAN GREPS, because the first version DID grep and reported build_engine_atlas.py as a parser of the alias ledger -- it only MENTIONS the filename in a comment. Comments and docstrings discuss registries constantly here, so a text scan measures prose density. The tool walks the AST and considers only string constants OUTSIDE docstrings, i.e. values the code computes with. THE INSTRUMENT THEN COUNTED ITSELF, reporting 17 -- it matched its own OWNED table across all three registries. That is ED-IN-0159 2.4 ('the instrument counted itself') recurring verbatim in a brand-new instrument, and it is worth more than the fix: a census whose CONFIGURATION names its own subject is self-matching by construction, and the only reliable defence is checking raw output for the tool's own name before believing a number. Honest baseline 14, not 17: 5 modules read references/restructure_ledger.md outside pathres, 6 read the editorial ledgers outside obs_core, 3 read id_reservations.yaml outside registry.py. Report-only and it REDS ON DAY ONE by design -- those 14 are the finding, not a regression, and blocking would refuse unrelated commits for a pre-existing condition (ED-IN-0112 paid for that once). WAVE 5 -- AND THE BRIEF'S ASSUMPTION WAS INVERTED BY MEASUREMENT. The wave plan said 'two carry the pre-change orphan set and will self-correct on their cron -- worth confirming rather than assuming'. Confirmed, and the real state is the other way round: FIVE of the six stale families are on the weekly audit-refresh cron and will self-correct; mechanics-index was on NOTHING. Its generator was wired into CI as `--strict`, which only VALIDATES and is warn-only, so drift was reported on every run and acted on by nobody -- 32 files behind. That is ED-IN-0159 1.6's shape one level up: not dead scope, but a LIVE SIGNAL WITH NO CONSUMER, which is decoration. Regenerated (502 insertions / 516 deletions) and added to the cron. THEN THE GUARD FOUND A SECOND ONE I HAD NOT LOOKED FOR, which is the argument for writing it: `glossary` also had no scheduled refresher. It read 'fresh, drift=0' purely because a previous session ran the generator by hand in fdbef6b -- a WORSE state than visible staleness, because the report said everything was fine. Both added to audit-refresh.yml. THE JOIN IS THE DELIVERABLE. tools/audit_staleness.py's FAMILIES had no field naming what refreshes each artifact, which is precisely why the gap was invisible; it could report six families stale and not say which of them anything would ever fix. Every family now declares a `refresher` (None = deliberately frozen, and it must be SAID), and tests/valoria/test_audit_refresh_coverage.py joins that declaration to the workflow in both directions -- the same shape broken_dependency_checker already applies between ci_checks_registry.yaml and valoria-ci.yml. The guard immediately caught my own fabricated filename: I guessed `tools/build_glossary.py` and the real path is tools/observability/build_glossary.py. MEASURED-BY: tools/single_owner_check.py -- `--check` prints the per-registry bypass list and its total against BASELINE=14; tools/audit_staleness.py prints the per-family drift and now the refresher for each. Both re-runnable. ⚠ CORRECTED 2026-08-13 (ED-IN-0181/0182, adversarial review): THIS ENTRY NARRATES A STATE THE TREE DOES NOT HAVE, and was not updated when the work was reverted hours later. Read it with these three corrections. (1) mechanics-index was regenerated and added to the cron -- BOTH WERE REVERTED. `--update` strips every comment from the register (39 -> 0, 5,081 chars); the regeneration was undone, the cron step removed, and the family now declares refresher=None. This entry's falsifier says the test fails 'if the mechanics-index step is dropped again'; the SHIPPED test asserts that step's ABSENCE. (2) 'Both added to audit-refresh.yml' was true of the glossary only in the sense that its GENERATOR was invoked -- `references/glossary/` was in neither the diff-check nor the `git add` list, so the cron regenerated the glossary in the runner and discarded it. The job would have gone green and the coverage guard would have reported the family covered. Fixed in ED-IN-0182 by adding the path to both lists AND by giving the guard an artifact-side leg. (3) The 14-bypass measurement stands, but the phrase 'modules that READ a registry directly' overclaims: at least two of the 14 are output-string MENTIONS (gen_audit:629, handoff_atomize:408), and glob-form reads are invisible to the scan. ⚠ FURTHER CORRECTION (ED-IN-0182 addendum): this entry's claim that glossary was 'fresh only by luck' is wrong. tests/valoria/test_build_glossary.py::test_committed_output_matches_a_fresh_build byte-compares the committed glossary against a fresh build inside the BLOCKING pytest suite, so corpus drift without regeneration fails the shipping gate. glossary is enforced-but-manual; mechanics-index was genuinely unenforced. Two different conditions, one label.
