title: The Wave 5 fix was DESTRUCTIVE: mechanics_index_gen --update strips every comment from the register it writes, and I scheduled it weekly before checking what it removed
description: SELF-REVERTED WITHIN ONE COMMIT, caught by the shipping gate rather than by me. Wave 5 (ED-IN-0180) found mechanics-index was the one stale family nothing refreshed, regenerated it with `tools/mechanics_index_gen.py --update`, and added that command to the weekly audit-refresh cron. The tool printed '[OK] Wrote drift_report back' and produced a 502-insertion / 516-deletion diff that looked plausible for a register 32 files behind. IT WAS NOT PLAUSIBLE, IT WAS DESTRUCTIVE. `--update` documents itself in --help as 'Write drift_report back into mechanics_index.yaml' -- a narrow write. What it actually does is round-trip the entire YAML through a loader/dumper, which SILENTLY STRIPS EVERY COMMENT. Measured against HEAD: 39 comment lines -> 0, 45,313 -> 40,232 characters, 5,081 characters of section headers and inline repointing rationale destroyed (the `notes:` FIELDS survived at 71 both sides, which is what made the diff look survivable at a glance -- the losses were all in comments, which no field-level check would see). Reverted; the cron step was added in 04e0289 and removed in the FOLLOWING commit, before it ever fired -- kept as two commits deliberately, because amending would have hidden that it was ever wired, and the fact that it looked correct enough to schedule IS the finding; mechanics-index now declares refresher=None WITH THE REASON at the declaration, and will keep reporting stale. That is honest: the drift is real and the fix is a code change making the generator comment-preserving, not a cron line. WHAT MAKES THIS WORSE THAN AN ORDINARY BUG, and why it is filed rather than quietly fixed: I was scheduling an UNATTENDED WEEKLY WRITE. It would have deleted hand-written prose every Monday, in an auto-opened PR nobody reads closely because 'it is just a regeneration', and the loss would have compounded silently. The generalisable rule: A FLAG'S DESCRIPTION IS NOT ITS EFFECT. Before scheduling any generator, run it once and diff for what it REMOVED, not only for what it wrote. HOW IT WAS CAUGHT, which is the part that worked: `pytest tests/valoria` went red on `test_no_retired_tree_pointers_remain_in_the_mechanics_index` -- and NOT because retired pointers appeared. The opposite: the regeneration deleted the excused occurrences that test used as its own positive control, so the guard failed with 'no excused occurrences found -- the two exclusions above are now untested'. A test written to prove it could tell a live pointer from a documented absence detected that its evidence had been destroyed. That is CLAUDE.md 0.1 point 2 paying out in an unanticipated direction. TWO SMALLER DEFECTS FOUND IN THE SAME GATE RUN, both mine and both the session's recurring class: (1) my first version of the recurrence assertion checked `'--update' not in workflow_text` and failed on the workflow's OWN COMMENT explaining why --update is absent -- prose about a thing counted as the thing, written minutes after I had recorded that exact class twice the same day (the grep-vs-AST fix in ED-IN-0180 and the 'ED-WR-0010 NOT allocated' false positive in ED-IN-0174). It is a persistent reflex, not a one-off. Now matches `run:` lines. (2) The duplicate-helper gate caught `workflow_text` and `_load` colliding with existing fixtures. These were NAME COLLISIONS, not shared logic -- my `workflow_text` reads audit-refresh.yml while test_compile_is_not_invocation's reads valoria-ci.yml, and `_load` is defined in 12 test modules each loading something different. Renamed to say what they are, which is the same idempotent-naming rule ED-IN-0179 established, applied at fixture scope. MEASURED-BY: registers/mechanics_index.yaml -- `git show HEAD~1:registers/mechanics_index.yaml` against the regenerated file gives the 39->0 comment-line count and the 5,081-character delta directly; tests/valoria/test_audit_refresh_coverage.py::test_mechanics_index_is_NOT_wired_because_its_generator_is_destructive pins that no mechanics_index_gen invocation returns to the cron.
falsifier: The comment-stripping claim is reproducible in one command: run `python3 tools/mechanics_index_gen.py --update` and count lines starting with '#' before and after. The recurrence guard fails if a mechanics_index_gen `run:` line reappears in audit-refresh.yml, and if mechanics-index declares a refresher again without proof the generator preserves comments.

title: Second adversarial review, with vocabulary as an explicit lens: a no-op fix, a harness measuring an unreachable classifier, a dead family row, and a blocking gate that cannot see engine/
description: Jordan asked whether Waves 3-5 had been audited against the new vocabulary convention. They had not -- the first Fable-5 review covered only Waves 1+2, and the convention (ED-IN-0179) was written AFTER it, so nothing had ever been checked against it, including Waves 4+5 which were the first work produced UNDER it. A read-only critic was run over all three commits with vocabulary as the primary lens. FIVE REAL DEFECTS, all fixed here. (1) MY GLOSSARY FIX WAS A NO-OP, AND WORSE THAN THE PROBLEM IT ADDRESSED. Wave 5 added build_glossary.py to the refresh cron but NOT references/glossary/ to the diff-check or `git add` lists, so the job regenerated the glossary inside the runner and discarded it. The run would have gone green and the new coverage guard would have reported the family COVERED, over a family still fresh only by luck -- a green light installed directly over the condition it was written to detect. RUNNING A GENERATOR IS NOT REFRESHING AN ARTIFACT. Both lists fixed; the guard gained a second leg asserting each refreshed artifact is actually committed, verified against a simulated pre-fix workflow line (the control reds on exactly the glossary row). The guard's own docstring had named this blind spot -- 'declaring a refresher the cron never invokes is the same blind spot with extra paperwork' -- one level up from where it then recurred. (2) THE FORK HARNESS MEASURES A CLASSIFIER THAT PRODUCTION NEVER REACHES, and this is the same trap it already recorded fixing once. Its docstring says it models 'the real code path, never a re-implementation' and warns 'model the decision, not the helper'. For broken_dependency_checker that boundary was still drawn too small: before any classification, bdc extracts candidate refs via extract_file_refs, whose tree roster is designs|systems|compilation|references|canon|tests|skills|tools (bdc:71-74) -- NO engine/, NO params/, NO audit/, NO registers/. Verified directly: `extract_file_refs` returns the EMPTY SET for engine/params/core.md, params/core.md and engine/anything_fabricated.md, and extracts systems/combat/combat_v30.md normally. So 3 of 4 probes never enter bdc at all and its reported verdicts are its classifier's, not its behaviour. gen_audit is the same shape (its real detection gates on _is_version_pointer first). The docstring is corrected to say which consumers are invoked and which are TRANSCRIBED. (3) AND THE BIGGER FINDING THAT FALLS OUT OF IT, which outranks everything Wave 3 reported: bdc is a BLOCKING gate whose stated job is separating a real citation from a fabricated one, and a live ledger entry citing a fabricated `engine/...` path extracts to nothing and passes SILENTLY. That is not a wrong verdict, it is the gate not looking. Reported and pinned by test_bdc_cannot_see_engine_paths_at_all, NOT fixed: widening a blocking gate's scope needs its own expected-delta test (CLAUDE.md 8). (4) THE npc-audit FAMILY POINTED AT AN EVACUATED ARTIFACT and had been silently reporting '(no data)'. audit/lane-a/ left main on 2026-08-05 and restructure_ledger.md:1319 carries it as FORK:c451bcb. Wave 5 EDITED THAT EXACT TABLE, added refresher=None calling it 'a frozen historical artifact', and pinned it in a test -- entrenching a dead row inside the commit whose whole subject was families whose reporting had quietly stopped meaning anything. Its own comment recorded an EARLIER repointing after the identical failure (from the retired designs/audit/ tree), onto a path evacuated two weeks later. RETIRED rather than repointed a third time, under the ED-IN-0163 rule: an absent path is dead only if its SUBJECT was retired, and here it was. New guard test_every_family_points_at_a_live_artifact makes the next one fail instead of going quiet. (5) `refresher: None` CARRIED TWO DISPOSITIONS -- the table header said it meant 'frozen historical artifact' while mechanics-index used it for 'blocked by a defect', and the test put both in one set named `frozen` with a comment saying one of them was not. One word, two meanings, inside the session that ruled vocabulary must be idempotent. Split into an explicit `no_refresher_because` field. THE VOCABULARY LENS ALSO JUDGED THE CONVENTION ITSELF, and found the headline wanting: 'idempotent' is a term of art for operations whose re-application changes nothing, NOT for a word whose meaning survives a cold read -- so the rule's own headline is a coinage, defined only by the 30-line body beneath it, which is the exact defect the rule describes. Left as-is pending Jordan (renaming a convention he authored is his call), but recorded. Terms judged RISKY: `refresher` (fixed), `bypass` (the word claims a read, the instrument measures a mention -- limits now recorded at the tool), `wave` (a pointer to session-local plan numbering that lives nowhere in the tree), `frozen` (three live senses). PASS: control, probe, ratchet, pair, hop, drift, harness, single owner, distinguishing, collapsed, family, baseline, join, fork row. ONE FALSE POSITIVE FROM THE REVIEW, and the fault is mine: it reported ED-IN-0181 as cited-but-never-allocated. It was allocated (next_free 182, row present); the critic read the working tree MID-EDIT because I ran a read-only audit against a tree I was actively modifying. Any finding from that run could have been stale, which is a process error to avoid repeating -- audit a committed ref, not a live tree. ⚠ SELF-CORRECTION, SAME DAY, FOUND BY THE SHIPPING GATE AND MISSED BY BOTH THE CRITIC AND ME: the claim that glossary was 'fresh only by luck' is WRONG, and it originated in ED-IN-0180. tests/valoria/test_build_glossary.py::test_committed_output_matches_a_fresh_build is a BLOCKING test in the shipping suite -- it rebuilds the glossary and byte-compares every committed file, so ANY corpus change that is not followed by a regeneration reds `pytest tests/valoria`. It fired on this very branch after my own edits. The glossary is therefore ENFORCED, not lucky; what it lacks is an UNATTENDED refresher, which is a different and much smaller gap. mechanics-index is the genuinely unenforced one: its only check is `--strict` in the warn-only validators-report tier, which reports and gates nothing. I conflated 'has no cron step' with 'has no enforcement' and stated the stronger claim for both. The cron step for glossary is still worth having -- it moves the work off the next author -- but it is convenience, not the closing of a hole, and the phrase 'worse than visible staleness' does not apply to it.

title: Five-lens read-only assessment: the designated authority surfaces are the rotten ones, and the ruling queue is polluted with SETTLED items that audits keep re-raising
description: Commissioned by Jordan 2026-08-13: assess structural rigour, vocabulary/formula standardization, modularity/injectability, and workflow compliance, across the repo and the recent waves. Method: five valoria-critic agents on Fable-5, Read/Grep/Glob only (structural independence, CLAUDE.md 10); four concurrent and blind to each other, a fifth given their four reports AS OUTPUT for throughlines/lessons/cull candidates. None could execute anything -- no pytest, no validator run, no git show -- so every gate-behaviour claim is read off source and no conclusion rests on an execution claim. SIX THROUGHLINES, ranked by independent-lens convergence. T1 (4 of 5, and the most reliable finding in the set): THE DESIGNATED AUTHORITIES ARE THE ROTTEN SURFACES. CURRENT.md:31 -- the section-1 priority-one currency index -- is one ~30,000-character line with roughly 8 reconcile-stamp blocks duplicated VERBATIM and a broken chronology, the signature of a mid-chain splice when the ED-IN-0151 stamp was inserted. THREE lenses found it independently. Same class: HANDOFF.md:47-49 (the only section the SessionStart banner reads) opens with a blocker resolved 2026-07-30 and holds nothing newer than July; glossary.md:45 bans and mandates `CI` in one sentence inside the self-declared canonical reference for term expansions; CLAUDE.md section 8 still lists supersession as blocking after it moved to the never-fails tier. The common mechanism: currency_consistency_check reads leading dates, MEASURED-BY requires a path to EXIST rather than to produce its number, validate_ed_citations:545 checks one ID family. Metadata validation everywhere, structural validation nowhere. T2 (4 of 5): OWNER DECLARED IN PROSE, ENFORCEMENT ABSENT. TN_STANDARD = 7 has three live definitions and NONE in its owner dice_engine.py, while the committed remediation plan prescribes `dice_engine.TN_STANDARD` -- a symbol that does not exist, a plan citing its own uncreated target. tools/single_owner_check.py is absent from ci_checks_registry.yaml ENTIRELY while invoked at valoria_local.py:242, so CLAUDE.md section 4's 'every tool has a role: line' is false as written, asserted in the same commit that shipped the violation. T3 (4 of 5): RATCHETS FREEZE DEBT AT DISCOVERY LEVEL -- a ratchet that may fall and never rise has no mechanism that makes it fall; measured across the wave the duplicate-reader count is unchanged at 14 while _load and bootstrap copies GREW, inside commits themed on single ownership. T4: the vocabulary failure reproduces inside its own fix -- one day after ED-IN-0179 settled evacuate/retire, a file named _archive became the primary allocation surface (ED-IN-0160..0182 exist only there); and `wave` fails both of Jordan's tests. T5 (5 of 5, NAMED BY NONE): THE JORDAN QUEUE IS THE STRUCTURAL BOTTLENECK -- every lens's worst duplication is ruled-but-not-executable or awaiting-ruling (dual mass-battle engines, attribute roster, Faction schema, sections 5-7, ED-IN-0163's landing site). No session can consolidate these; the fan-out keeps re-measuring them. The cheapest single intervention is a BATCHED RULING SESSION, not another audit wave -- and this assessment is itself an instance of the pattern it names. T6 (3 of 5): tests/ is the largest ungoverned surface -- 159 sys.path.insert across 131 files while conftest.py does no path setup. FIVE LESSONS, L1 being the highest-priority class: rules ALREADY WRITTEN and still not followed -- section 0.1 point 5's guard rule is applied per incident, not per pattern; of five named recurring patterns exactly one has a guard. L3: a count is admissible only if a reader with grep reproduces it -- demonstrated both ways, since an independent agent reproduced the armature census (1,859 occurrences / 263 files) exactly in one grep, while the 32-term / ~26,000-use census now baked into CLAUDE.md section 4 as this convention's motivation CANNOT be reproduced from the tree. CULL CANDIDATES sorted by the ED-IN-0163 rule into SAFE TO CULL / CONSOLIDATE / LOOKS DEAD BUT KEEP / NEEDS A RULING, with the caution cases live: audit/ instruments are pinned by SHIPPED TESTS, so evacuating audit/ per the classifier breaks a test. DISAGREEMENTS RECORDED NOT SMOOTHED, including one finding OVERTURNED (lens A's parity-oracle citation: that test no longer imports the audit oracle, it reads a committed golden specifically to remove the coupling -- the finding survives on one leg). THREE THINGS ALL FOUR MISSED: workplan_v6_progress.yaml is a month stale and its own anti-rot rule watches two RETIRED trees; godot/ got zero examination despite being the port target, with GO next_free still 1 (no Godot ED ever allocated) and an unfilled Status template outside the parse window; and patch_register_active.yaml holds 6 entries whose header points at archive files that no longer exist. MEASURED-BY: audit/2026-08-14-five-lens-repo-assessment/00_findings.md carries every claim with file:line; the reproducible ones are re-runnable by grep and are marked as such, and the claims requiring execution are marked inferred and are load-bearing on nothing. ⚠ CORRECTION FROM JORDAN, IN SESSION 2026-08-14, AND IT SHARPENS T5 RATHER THAN ILLUSTRATING IT. All five lenses reported the mass-battle situation as an open canon question. IT IS NOT AND HAS NOT BEEN SINCE 2026-08-03. Jordan, verbatim: 'I've ruled on mass battle like eighteen times. It's the one with a huge amount of code and the target of loads of commits, not the tiny shit one that kept being used in simulations with opposing military rolls.' MEASURED so no future session can mistake the identity: tests/sim/mass_battle/ is 11,269 lines across ~30 modules (engine, geometry, perimeter, percell, contact, exchange, attrition, troop_types, equipment, validators, provenance) -- the big one, the commit target, CANON. systems/mass_battle/sim/ is 2,385 lines of which massbattle.py is a single 1,905-line god-module -- the small one, retired. J2 is ALREADY RECORDED CORRECTLY at systems/mass_battle/sim/__init__.py:1-11. The audits re-raised a settled question because CURRENT.md narrates the J2-vs-keep-pin tension twice verbatim and prior audit prose repeats 'dual engines' without saying the canon question is CLOSED. THE ACTUAL BLOCKER IS NARROW AND IS NOT ABOUT MASS BATTLE: migrating faction_action.py:431 onto the canon engine is blocked on ruling the four `degree` band edges (__init__.py:8-9) -- one bounded question, and Lens B measured that 8 of 11 degree sites are mergeable with NO ruling, leaving only faction_action.py:97 (45% band divergence) needing the call. SO T5 HAS A SECOND HALF NOBODY NAMED: the ruling queue is not only long, it is POLLUTED WITH SETTLED ITEMS THAT KEEP BEING RE-RAISED, and re-raising a settled ruling costs more than leaving one unruled -- it consumes the ruler's attention and teaches sessions that rulings do not stick.

The overturned finding (A-F7's parity-oracle citation) is recorded as overturned rather than deleted. Grades are deliberately NOT averaged across lenses -- D5 records why.

title: Contradiction hunt: CLAUDE.md scoped philosophy compliance to P-14 while canon has defined P-15 since April -- a SILENT miss in the governing document, plus 7 more conflicts
description: A sixth read-only Fable-5 lens, commissioned by Jordan and pointed at conflicts and contradictions only, over surfaces the five-lens assessment barely touched (systems/ design docs, canon/, Status lines, ledger-vs-index). Eight contradictions ranked by blast radius on a cold reader, five suspects DISSOLVED on inspection and recorded as dissolved. FINDING 1, FIXED HERE, AND THE WORST KIND -- SILENT, IN THE GOVERNING DOCUMENT. CLAUDE.md said 'P-01..P-14' in three places including section 9's routing row for valoria-canon-guard, the skill whose entire job is philosophy compliance. canon/02_canon_constraints.md:24 has defined P-15 since 2026-04-02 (three-layer being-persistence, Leap vulnerability window, Coherence-0 TS branching) and it carries a real FAIL test; canon/00_philosophical_foundations_rules.md:5,104 says P-01 through P-15; four skills scope themselves to P-15; systems/threadwork/sim/coherence.py implements it by name. THE FAILURE MODE IS SILENCE: a compliance pass scoped by section 9 audits fourteen constraints, never looks at P-15, and reports 'all principles checked'. Nothing errors. CLAUDE.md section 3 defers world/design truth to canon/, so canon wins and the governing doc was four months stale. MEASURED REPO-WIDE: 13 understating occurrences across 11 files. NINE fixed on live surfaces (CLAUDE.md x3, CURRENT.md x2, canon/README.md, systems/_architecture/ x4, tools/ x2). FOUR deliberately NOT fixed -- three editorial ledgers and one dated audit unit are HISTORICAL RECORDS of what was believed at the time, and rewriting them would violate the same no-retrofit posture as the ED-<LANE>-NNNN cutover and the flat-ED freeze. The guard is scoped to live surfaces for that reason. SECOND GUARD SHIPPED, covering three more of the eight: a doc may not carry two `## Status:` lines in the 80-line head window, because the G8 single owner takes the FIRST match -- so a second Status line is not a conflict the tooling resolves, it is a line the tooling CANNOT SEE while a human reading the file sees it perfectly. Measured: 5 instances, of which 3 are genuine contradictions (derived_stats_v30 CANONICAL vs a PROPOSAL that supersedes the file it appears in, and that doc is the Truth-Track SoT and the combat wound constants' authority; faction_canon_v30 CANONICAL vs PROVISIONAL where the PROVISIONAL line redirects authority to four other documents, an ED-1094 flip that never happened; character_generation_questionnaire_v30 CANONICAL vs 'not yet authored'), 1 dissolved and 1 unassessed. Ratchet, not conformance gate. NOT FIXED, HELD FOR JORDAN -- the remaining findings are design-content calls, not mechanical: (a) systems/combat/combat_reference_v1.md:218,347 -- a doc CREATED 2026-08-08 by the ED-PC-0056 5->1 consolidation re-publishes WI = End+6 with no Max-Wounds cap, a formula superseded for ~7 weeks, TWICE, one of them in the same sentence as its citation to derived_stats_v30.md:20, which says WI = round(End + 4 + 0.4 x Spirit) with MW cap 3 -- matching the engine (combatant.py:20-37, 'Jordan 2026-06-18: flat base lowered 6->4'). Anyone porting or balancing from the consolidated reference gets Health wrong for every combatant and the byte-exact engine tests never see it, because the error lives only in the doc. (b) CURRENT.md:156 says 'Retires ED-921' while registers/editorial_ledger.jsonl:169 has ED-921 status open -- and the same sentence retains a baseline PENDING the ID it retires, so the retirement condition can never be evaluated and the 'temporary' bare-roll baseline is permanent by construction. (c) 'Piety Track' is defined at personal scale by conviction_track_v1.md:8-12 and at per-territory scale by conviction_track_v30.md:22-25, against ED-IN-0075 which renamed the character-scale meter to Truth and staged the 419-ref sweep that was never executed. (d) CURRENT.md cites engine/params/core.md as a live SoT location at :154 while marking it EVACUATED at :168. AND A JARGON CORRECTION FROM JORDAN, same session: I wrote that the mass-battle migration was blocked on 'ruling the four degree band edges', copied verbatim from systems/mass_battle/sim/__init__.py:8-9. Jordan: 'this doesn't mean anything in English'. Correct -- coined jargon propagated by copying a source comment instead of translating it, the exact failure CLAUDE.md 4 legislates against, committed one day after that section was written. Translated at BOTH sites into the two plain questions it actually names: when a faction takes a strategic action, is 'how well did it go' judged against how hard the action was or against fixed numbers (canon scales to difficulty at dice_engine.py:94-122; faction_action._degree:97-104 uses fixed cutoffs); and does scraping exactly zero count as a partial success or a failure (canon says failure, faction_action says partial -- same number, opposite outcome). title: Post-assessment remediation plan: 5 tracks, 12 burn-down steps, and a 7-question batched ruling agenda -- with a rule that a guard may only land beside a burn-down
description: Decomposition by a read-only Fable-5 planner (CLAUDE.md 10 assigns planning to the top tier), written up by Opus. Plans against audit/2026-08-14-five-lens-repo-assessment/00_findings.md. THE RULE THAT MAKES IT DIFFERENT, and it exists because of finding T3: a step may add a guard ONLY in the same commit as a burn-down of the thing it guards, and every ratchet it touches must leave with a LOWER pinned maximum than it entered with. Twelve steps are marked [BURN]. If the burn-downs are skipped and the guards land, THE PLAN HAS FAILED BY ITS OWN STANDARD -- that is the falsifier for the plan as a whole, not just its parts. This session earned the rule: it added three instruments and the single-owner bypass count did not move. FIVE TRACKS, parallelisable across lanes. A -- authority repair: de-duplicate CURRENT.md:31 WITH the structural check in the same commit, fix HANDOFF.md's banner section, the CI sentence, and two false rows. A2 also fixes T5's pollution half, because the same dedupe removes the twice-verbatim J2 narration that made five independent lenses report a settled Jordan ruling as an open question. B -- owner enforcement: TN_STANDARD into dice_engine, the bare-RNG sweep with its guard, 8 of 11 degree sites merged with NO ruling required, single_owner_check registered. C -- gate perimeter: validate_ed_citations extended to audit/'s 2,612 unscanned citations and broken_dependency_checker widened to engine/, both with the pre-change control both are blocking gates. D -- tests/ governance: the conftest bootstrap AS THE LEANNESS PLAN'S OWN NOT-STARTED T5 rather than a fork of it, the ~39-block slice not the 131-file corpus. E -- boards, godot, vocabulary, and the combat doc transcription fix. SEVEN QUESTIONS FOR ONE RULING SESSION, each in plain English with options and costs: CURRENT.md reduction (both branches pre-built so it executes same-day), the two faction-scoring calls, d6-vs-d10 strategic dice, the PP citation system, ledger overflow naming, godot lane on-or-dormant, and Q7 which asks only that the attribute roster and Faction schema be SCHEDULED as workshops rather than answered in the session. THE PLANNER CORRECTED THE BRIEF: Faction's port-blocking declaration is at engine/autoload/game_state.py:6-11, not under systems/factions/sim/ as I had written. SIX CLAIMS ARE MARKED INFERRED rather than verified -- the ED-921 ledger line, the 11-site degree list, the armature referents, combat_engine_v1/config.py's WI constant, dice_engine's import graph, and _kernel_tests.py's importer set -- and each carries a hard executor-side precondition so the inference is tested before it is acted on. E3 states outright that if the engine implements End+6 the step inverts. 'Deliberately not planned' is a real section with reasons, not a disclaimer: the canon mass-battle engine's RNG unification, the full 419-ref Piety-to-Truth sweep, module_contracts enforcement and combat_engine_v1 repackaging are each named, and most are blocked behind a ruling -- which is T5 again. MEASURED-BY: audit/2026-08-14-five-lens-repo-assessment/01_plan.md carries every step's falsifier as the command or test the executing session runs; nothing in it was executed at planning time and it says so.
falsifier: The plan's own whole-plan falsifier is stated in it: if the [BURN] steps are skipped and the guard steps land, it failed. Per-step falsifiers are commands/tests for the executing session. The six inferred claims each carry a precondition that must be checked before the step proceeds.

title: A test whose verdict depended on whether the author had uncommitted work -- it measured the environment, not the subject, and only surfaced on a clean tree
description: test_the_gate_still_runs_and_still_reports (pre-existing, from #305 / ED-IN-0160) ran tools/ci_co_file_checker.py in --local mode against the AMBIENT WORKING TREE and asserted the gate produced a report line. Its input was therefore 'whatever the author happened to have uncommitted'. On a CLEAN tree the gate correctly prints 'No changed files detected. Skipping co-file check.' and the assertion fails. THE TEST PASSED OR FAILED BASED ON WHETHER YOU HAD UNSAVED WORK, which is the one thing it was not trying to measure. WHY IT WENT UNNOTICED FOR NINE DAYS: a session almost always runs the suite mid-change, so the ambient tree almost always has changed files. It surfaced only when the suite was run against a fully committed and pushed tree -- which is the state CI is closest to, and which this session reached only after committing, merging and pushing everything. Four earlier full-suite runs the same session reported 1905 passed BECAUSE the tree was dirty at the time; the fifth, on the clean pushed state, went red. I had already reported green from those runs. FIX: the same deterministic temp-repo technique the sibling test test_rule_1_actually_REJECTS_a_changeset_it_must_reject already uses in this very file -- build a real git repo, stage a COMPLIANT changeset (design doc AND its canonical_sources co-file moving together), run the gate in --staged mode, and require it to run and report. The non-vacuity intent is unchanged; only its input is now controlled instead of borrowed. Added assertion: 'Skipping' must NOT appear, so if the gate's change detection ever breaks against a changeset that genuinely has changed files, this fails -- the defect class the test exists for. THE GENERAL FORM, which is this session's recurring lesson in a new place: A TEST WHOSE VERDICT DEPENDS ON AMBIENT ENVIRONMENT MEASURES THE ENVIRONMENT, NOT THE SUBJECT. The same shape as ED-IN-0181's vacuous allowlist (passed because its corpus emptied) and ED-IN-0182's no-op glossary refresh (green because nothing checked the artifact) -- a green result produced by the wrong cause.
falsifier: The fix is verified by the condition that produced the failure: the test now passes on a CLEAN tree (git status empty), which is exactly where the old version failed. The added 'Skipping' assertion fails if change detection breaks on a changeset that has changed files.
